The European Competitiveness Fund, the Backbone of a Modern European Investment Policy

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • European businesses call for a robust, well-funded European Competitiveness Fund.
  • Europe is losing ground in technological leadership and struggles to scale strategic technologies, while volatile energy costs and external dependencies continue to dampen business confidence.
  • Sources indicate that europe’s path to enduring technological leadership relies on our ability to scale strategic technologies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European businesses call for a robust, well-funded European Competitiveness Fund.

Dear Chancellors, Prime Ministers, Presidents,.

Europe is losing ground in technological leadership and struggles to scale strategic technologies, while volatile energy costs and external dependencies continue to dampen business confidence.

Sources indicate that europe’s path to enduring technological leadership relies on our ability to scale strategic technologies. By stabilising energy costs, providing a path to clean industrial renewal and cultivating European resilience, we are laying the groundwork for robust business and investors’ confidence. Public investment has a crucial role to play to address these vital challenges. We require a smarter, more strategic investment policy for Europe.

Industry observers note that we, more than 75 undersigned businesses, call on European leaders to agree to a Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) commensurate with Europe’s challenges, to protect its investment capacity and place long-term productivity growth, resilience and decarbonisation at its core. We believe the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF) represents a step-change in the EU’s investment policy and must be strengthened in the remaining negotiations.

The ECF with its toolbox projects the ambition to provide tailored support to the investment and scale-up challenge Europe faces. This is a positive evolution of the EU funding landscape. With a bigger role for the EU’s derisking instrument InvestEU, the ECF can become Europe’s modern investment vehicle with an increased use of guarantees, loans and equity to unlock strategic investments.

At the same time, non-repayable support needs to be dedicated to scaling up sectors that deliver high strategic value but cannot yet secure commercial capital in Europe. Ramp-up support for Europe’s cleantech manufacturing, including support for OpEx, is needed to make Europe’s bid to regain technological leadership credible.

It has been revealed that the advisory services for SMEs and the single access portal promises a simpler access to funding for firms across Europe. If successful, the ECF can pool additional national funds through merit-based procedures open to eligible projects across the single market to bring further alignment and synergies into European industrial development.

Recent findings suggest that europe’s energy import dependency has become a strategic vulnerability for European businesses. To increase our economic resilience, the EU must prioritise investments into energy sovereignty. Incentives need to pivot capital allocation away from fossil fuel infrastructure, and towards clean energy and electrification. From 2028, the next MFF should not support new fossil-fuel infrastructure that prolongs dependency on fossil fuels, while providing narrowly defined safeguards for security of supply. We need steering mechanisms to reduce fossil fuel dependencies. EU funding can help to tackle high upfront costs and derisk the switch to cleaner and more reliable energy. Otherwise, long investment cycles create severe fossil fuel lock-in effects that threaten our operational autonomy with increasingly volatile fossil energy prices.

It has been revealed that europe’s investment gap cannot be solved by a smarter, more strategic funding approach alone. The confidence into European competitiveness needs to translate into a sizable budget for the clean transition to have lasting impact. The Commission proposes an average annual budget of €3.3 billion for a clean transition and industrial decarbonisation window of the ECF. This number is dwarfed by recurring estimates of the annual climate investment deficit of €344 billion. At the same time, according to the OECD, industrial subsidies have reached the highest levels since the financial crisis 2008.

We urge European leaders to respond to the evolving investment environment and adopt the European Parliament’s proposal to increase the size of the ECF by €26.6 billion and to allocate a substantial share of the additional funding for industrial decarbonisation and clean transition. The more efficient use of financial instruments and a strategic prioritisation can improve the impact of EU funding but cannot substitute the investment needs Europe is facing to boost competitiveness and security.

The next long-term budget and the European Competitiveness Fund must become the investment trigger for European businesses to regain competitiveness at the global scale, based on clear incentives and regulatory certainty. We businesses urge leaders to demonstrate a long-term vision and make the ECF the cornerstone of a latest EU green industrial strategy.

Download the letter to see the full list of signatories.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that happy Tuesday! It's November 24, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift — your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most vital stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.

In this morning's edition we're looking at the Department of Defense getting GM and Ford into the drone business, and Tesla pushing its driver assistance on the elderly. We'll also look at Volkswagen's battle against its workers, and Ineos moving stateside.

Under the Trump administration, the United States government has shifted from a focus on soft power — international aid, alliances, things of that nature — to focusing entirely on hard military power. Gone are the days of USAID, now is the era of massing drones. Only, there's a problem: U.S. drone makers can't actually make enough to keep up with Department of Defense orders. Thus, a new push from the Pentagon, to get automakers into the drone business. From the Wall Street Journal:.

The Pentagon is in talks with General Motors and other manufacturers to help mass produce drones, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest effort by the U.S. military to enlist the car industry's sprawling assembly lines to increase production of critical munitions and equipment.

In a recent development, under a deal, auto companies would supply parts to drone companies, the people said. Among the scenarios: GM is weighing whether to manufacture drone motors, albeit closer in size to something that would power a riding lawn mower than a car. Defense officials have met with leaders at Ford Motor, Canadian parts giant Magna International and other manufacturing companies, including outside the auto industry.

Responses from automakers around drone building have been "mixed," according to the WSJ, but we live in an era where the President can hand-pick who runs companies in spite of all manner of allegations. Do we really think any U.S.-based tech giant in its right mind would say no to such a man? Maybe an automaker could stall until the new legislative session in January, but that doesn't remove Trump from power.

Tesla doesn't so much care about selling its cars as it does selling its software these days, and the company seems to have its sights set on a latest frontier of driver-assistance software: The elderly. If you're wondering what happens when you combine technology that lulls drivers into a false sense of security with drivers whose reflexes and powers of perception are failing them, well, we're about to find out. From Bloomberg:.

Industry observers note that tesla warns consumers that FSD requires drivers to pay attention and be prepared to take immediate action at all times. It acknowledges none of its driver-assistance features make Teslas autonomous. And yet the firm is increasingly promoting the merits of the system to seniors, further muddling the already complex question of when the moment has come for older drivers to give up their car keys.

Experts say the technology's limitations may actually raise risks for the elderly. The pitfalls of aging, including changes in vision, loss of physical mobility and slower reflexes, can impair an older driver's ability to safely take control when needed.

The core issue here is a thorny one. On the one hand, seniors still need to get around — grocery delivery isn't always an option on a fixed income, and socializing staves off dementia. On the other hand, people whose faculties are decaying probably shouldn't be controlling thousands of pounds of metal that hurtle through our roads, especially with software that only demands occasional-yet-immediate engagement rather than constant attention. The answer is buses, but no one wants to talk about that.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen, one of the world's largest carmakers, thinks it's too big. To compete with lower-cost competitors from China, the organization is trying to scale back its own costs — by cutting production and people. Those people are, understandably, not super psyched about these decisions. From Reuters:.

EMDEN, Germany, Nov 24 (Reuters) – Volkswagen began crunch ‌wage talks with labour representatives on Tuesday amid mounting worker anger over deep cost cuts, with protesters carrying black coffins to symbolise what they noted was the death of trust and the company's future prospects.

The first round of talks takes place in the northern German ​town of Emden, home to one of the factories fighting for survival, where around 4,000 workers protested before representatives of the IG Metall ​union ad the automaker's works council met Volkswagen management.

"If necessary, there will also be industrial action of a kind never before seen at Volkswagen," works council head Daniela Cavallo told workers chanting "strike-ready" and carrying black coffins inscribed with the words "future" and "trust".

According to recent reports, when your workers start carrying coffins around to show the long-term costs of your short-sighted decision making, it's probably worth listening to them. Volkswagen's idea to cut its staff and production capacity to the bone is the sort of move that works on a spreadsheet, but realistically hampers the tech giant's ability to be agile in a market that's seen constant changes from shifting international regulations and fresh competitors. Essentially, the company is looking to specialize in doing things in a way that works right now, with the hope that the current circumstances never change.

Ineos, a firm I occasionally remember exists and is real, wants to sell in the U.S. without tariffs. To do so, it's looking to start production on our shores, and it's going to make the numbers work by getting rid of one of its European factories — specifically, by selling a French factory to BYD. From Automotive News:.

Ineos Automotive, hampered by President Donald Trump's import tariffs, is ready to build in the U.S.

The small British automaker said it has identified a short list of U.S. sites where it plans to produce pickups and SUVs. At the same time the organization, in a major pivot, plans to sell its French assembly plant to Chinese automaker BYD.

The two moves would have major repercussions on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean: Ineos would gain a manufacturing footprint in the country where it generates 70 percent of its global sales, and BYD would collect another European plant.

Industry observers note that this is the kind of knock-on effect that's hard to predict when you institute tariffs. Sure, production of the Ineos Grenadier expands into the U.S., and that plays well with the UAW folks from whom Trump wants votes, it also enables a further BYD foothold in Europe, though, emboldening a Chinese competitor that Trump would rather see quashed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) is an interesting piece of legislation. It is getting a ton of support from the solar sector, but it is heavily opposed by environmental organizations.

In a recent development, following the passage of BAAJA in the US Senate the other day, Tim Pawlenty, CEO of the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA), stated the following: “America is now one step closer to lower energy costs, more clean energy and a more reliable electric grid. Senators Lee, Capito, Heinrich, and Whitehouse deserve tremendous credit for advancing this bipartisan bill.”.

According to recent reports, the organization adds some more detail and why it thinks this is such a good piece of legislation: “SEIA analysis reveals that BAAJA could unlock 167 gigawatts of additional solar capacity between 2028 and 2035, bringing solar to over 18% of U.S. electricity generation by 2035. The analysis finds that the bill’s reforms could reduce cumulative power sector CO2 emissions by approximately 20% and avoid $54 billion in public health damages.”.

Industry observers note that that sounds very appealing, doesn’t it? Why wouldn’t we want that?

Sources indicate that well, the Sierra Club argues the bill goes in quite the opposite direction. The storied organization states the following: “While a rogue president is waging a war on clean energy, the Senate rushed a deeply flawed bill that furthers the buildout of fossil fuels, strips away power from communities and Tribes, threatens our clean water and public lands, and endangers wildlife. The House of Representatives has an equal voice in the legislative process. They must reject the Senate’s fast-tracked bill and demand debate and consideration to deliver for the people, not corporate polluters and Donald Trump. The American people made a clear call merely weeks ago: our elected leaders must address soaring costs and a corrupt system that prioritizes corporate polluter profits over our health, our wallets, and our future.”.

It has been revealed that it seems the concern is that BAAJA would make it much easier to put up power plants, skipping all kinds of environmental protections. That is why Republicans support it in the first place — they are always keen to plow through environmental protections. The reason SEIA supports it is clear enough — the organization is just thinking about solar power plants and looking at the potential for more growth in the industry, especially considering the fact that solar is now typically the cheapest option for newly introduced power capacity and has been dominating new installations.

So, the question is: would BAAJA really disproportionately support solar power, or would it lead to a lot more fossil fuel power plants and an edge to the old, dirty power technologies? Can the legislation be both good and bad, or is someone getting this wrong?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Verra, an artificial intelligence startup building the institutional memory layer for consulting firms, noted today it has raised $5 million in seed funding to help those companies overcome their amnesia and make their decades of knowledge accessible to every employee.

Today’s round was led by Kearny Jackson and saw participation from Andreessen Horowitz’s a16z Speedrun, Petra and a number of strategic investors. It comes just seven months after Verra, officially known as Lighthouse Software Technologies Inc., released its platform.

Industry observers note that verra was founded last year by Chief Executive Kashyap Nathan (pictured, right), who previously worked as a researcher at OpenAI Group PBC and Palantir Technologies Inc., and Christopher Farrington (left), a former software engineer at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Ltd. In an interview, Nathan explained that he and Farrington had seen firsthand how well-paid consultants would struggle with upcoming customer engagements, wasting hours of time researching to surface institutional knowledge that their tech giant already possessed.

“Consulting firms sit on decades of proposals, models and reports, and almost none of it is usable by the people who need it next,” Nathan noted. “We built the layer that makes that knowledge usable, and we built it to run inside the firm’s own cloud, because no consulting firm is going to send client work to a shared service.”.

Sources indicate that verra makes consulting firms’ institutional knowledge accessible through an artificial intelligence-native memory layer that indexes their past deliverables and distills their previous methodologies into reusable skills for autonomous agents. Then, those agents can utilize those skills to get started in tools such as Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Excel, and generate a highly detailed draft for latest client engagements in ten hours or less.

Nathan noted that’s a major improvement. At most consulting firms, it typically takes about 80 hours to get that first draft ready. “The traditional approach involves a SharePoint search box and a junior analyst with a week to spare,” he explained. “The AI-native version of that is a chat tool that answers a question from a few retrieved pages and leaves the consultant to rewrite the output. But both start from a blank page.”.

Verra is also much more efficient, Nathan mentioned. Whereas traditional chatbots can generate text snippets, Verra creates its sourced deliverables directly inside Office files that will be organized alongside the client brief.

In a recent development, “Verra starts from the firm. It indexes everything the firm has produced, distills how each practice does its work, and then lets a consultant point at a new situation and get to most of a finished deliverable in Excel or PowerPoint, before the human analyst starts writing a line,” Nathan said. “Every claim links to the page or cell it came from. The firm’s engineers and ours then build the specific workflows a team wants.”.

The architecture of Verra’s agents is important, too. The firm built them to run inside client’s clouds after looking at three realities of the professional services business. Consulting firms cannot allow their client’s data to leave their own environments, they will not trust an answer that can’t be verified, and AI will not be used if it forces them to drop the tools and systems they’re already using.

According to recent reports, it’s this approach that has been the secret to Verra’s promising early adoption. Its agents are already being used by two major global consulting firms in Berkeley Research Group and The Keystone Group. In the case of the former, more than 90% of its consultants are using Verra daily, and have generated more than 105,000 files since August while replacing the Tableau platform with a natural-language Snowflake interface. Berkeley calculates that Verra’s platform has helped the company to save around 215,000 analyst hours annually.

Recent findings suggest that “Verra hands our teams finished, sourced first drafts on engagements that used to start from a blank page,” stated Berkeley’s global managing director of AI solutions, Raghav Vadlamani. “It has changed how quickly we move for clients.”.

Moving forward, Nathan wants to integrate Verra’s AI agents even deeper with the consulting firms it serves, so they can learn how the entire manufacturer works and improve its overall efficiency rather than just focusing on one engagement at a time. He also sees an opportunity to move into adjacent sectors such as investment research and accounting. He wants to give customers’ engineers a way to build on Verra’s platform too.

Kearny Jackson Partner Sriram Krishnan stated he used to work in the consulting industry himself and that he’s all too familiar with the rinse-and-repeat process that accompanies each new client engagement. “What stood out to us was how swiftly Verra became critical to the firms using it,” he said. “Their consultants adopt it, use it and demand more of it. It’s becoming the memory and operating layer for how consulting firms work.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that "Grand Theft Auto 6" has been out for over a week at this point, so if you play it, you're probably well acquainted with the seemingly endless number of cars you can drive in the game. However, like all GTA games, none of them are real. Sure, they're all pretty close to what we get in the real world, but they're not exactly one-to-one. There are plenty of reasons why that is, but it can still leave ya (read: me) wishing that there were some real cars in the game, and that idea is what led me to the question I asked you all last week.

In a recent development, I wanted to know what real cars you'd want to be able to drive in "Grand Theft Auto 6". For the most part, you folks played along, giving me real answers, and I do appreciate that. Some of you wieners, however, decided that it would be a good time to let everyone know you don't play video games, and I'd like to be the first person to say, you are so, so interesting. Can I kiss you on the mouth? Because no one has ever been cooler than you. They should give you an award.

In any case, why don't ya scroll on down below and check out what real cars your fellow Jalpos wish they could drive in "GTA 6," and if you need to reiterate that you aren't interested in GTA and you don't play video games, please kick rocks with open-toed shoes.

A 1974 Dodge Monaco with a cop motor, a 440 cubic inch plant, cop tires, cop suspension, and cop shocks. It should be a model made before catalytic converters so it'll run good on regular gas.

Sources indicate that A Japanese dekotora truck. I wished for one in GTA 5 Online. It's wild, unique, and would fit right in driving down Ocean Drive at night.

It has been revealed that it was cool in GTA V when they had an Abarth 500 because I love the RL car so much. But one thing that constantly eluded the car nerds in GTA was the Miata (minus the Mañana from LCS), and at this point I'd love any generation. For a game that honors cars so well, I'm shocked they didn't make even the NA, a car with a cult-like following, nicknamed "The Answer" by so many car enthusiasts, and available in any respectable (and un-respectable) racing title you can think of, and yet more niche stuff has entered the game before the Miata did.

I think a Miata would fit right in driving around Vice City.

Submitted by: Drift on Air & TN Cyclist.

According to recent reports, an Audi RS6 avant would be nice for all the errands. Come to think f it there are no Audis in the game when they ubiquitous in GTAV.

In a recent development, MINE! I've driven down to Miami a couple times with my 968, and what I'm looking forward to most is re-creating some of the photos I've taken down there.

It has been revealed that I don't expect to find a 968 clone in game, but they've got to at least have a 928 clone. The Scarface reference is right there.

If I played any video games at all – for GTA I would want to drive a car that I have personally owned, so my choice is between a 1979 Ford LTD 2dr coupe with the 351ci V8 and a 1994 GEO Metro XFi with a 50 hp 1L 3cyl.

It has been revealed that did a little digging to see what vehicle can be easy (but ungodly expensive) to purchase, register, and take care of everything the GTA games are known for. Besides, with this kind of truck, I'll have it paid off pretty quickly after a few quick hits. It's the Alpine Armoring MASTIFF Limited Edition. It's a counter-terrorism, extreme-threat customized Ford pickup, and it can stop up to .50 caliber BMG rounds. It does cost over $400,000 though, but how much is my life worth? Plus it looks durable enough for those high speed chases down the beach, causing beachgoers to flee and umbrellas to burst into confetti. There's plenty of room for massive bags of cash, my associates, and enough weaponry to take over a small European country.

A cargo delivery van, just imagine how many flowers you could buy for her.

One of these lil guys. Just for the fun.

Sources indicate that there are so many IRL cars that I only came to love after seeing their GTA equivalents. I'd never seen or heard of the R32-R34 Nissan Skylines until I saw the Elegy Retro Custom in GTA Online. I also thought the Sabre Turbo looked stupid until I dechromed the rear bumper and thought, "okay that looks rad" — it's based on the Oldsmobile Cutlass and 442. Also, I loved the Ford Falcon XB from Mad Max before seeing its derivative in GTA Online, so as soon as the Apocalypse Imperator came out I bought it.

Industry observers note that I don't think I'd want to actually drive any particular IRL cars in GTA 6 without the ability to substantially customize and mod them though, especially if the "base civilian version" is boring and anemic compared to the cars the game pushes you toward driving. Filling a garage with your "favorite cars" but never being able to really drive them beyond RP purposes kinda sucks.

None, I've almost never been satisfied by driving a hero car of mine on a video game. They always end up being way too fast and uncontrollable or feel stupidly slow because they're old. Especially cars I've driven/owned, every one I've been able to drive in a game has been unsatisfying. I'd much rather develop favorites in-game as I play than pine for certain cars to be added.

The LiTime Lares K1 Expandable Plug & Play Kitchen Backup — CleanTechnica Tested

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I spent 35 years in the Tampa suburbs, so I pay attention to backup power when a storm  is coming.
  • It has been revealed that liTime introduced the Lares K1 in the US on October 20, 2026.
  • The inverter puts out 2,000 watts continuously and 4,000 watts of surge power for one second, as a pure sine wave at 120 volts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I spent 35 years in the Tampa suburbs, so I pay attention to backup power when a storm  is coming. Last year I tested the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 portable power station for CleanTechnica. That unit is meant to be carried around. The LiTime Lares K1 is different: a plug-in kitchen backup battery you leave in place and hook up to a refrigerator and also use to power your small kitchen appliances. First I’ll go through the specs and how it compares with a portable station like the Elite 100 V2, then I’ll give my test results.

It has been revealed that liTime introduced the Lares K1 in the US on October 20, 2026. It is a split system: a slim inverter charger paired with a separate 2,304 watt-hour LiFePO4 battery (51.2 volts, 45 amp-hours). You can add up to four batteries, which brings the total to 9,216 watt-hours. The battery is rated for 4,000 cycles, and LiTime backs it with a 5-year warranty.

The inverter puts out 2,000 watts continuously and 4,000 watts of surge power for one second, as a pure sine wave at 120 volts. Adding batteries does not raise that output. You just get more runtime. There are two AC outlets, one on each side of the inverter. I did not see any USB ports listed.

Sources indicate that you can charge it at up to 1,500 watts from a wall outlet and up to 800 watts from solar (12 to 60 volts). Combined input is capped at 1,500 watts. LiTime does not put a charge time on the main product page. If you divide 2,304 watt-hours by the 1,500-watt wall input, you get about 90 minutes from empty to full. That is a rough estimate. Charging usually slows down as you get close to 100%, the same way an EV does, and their FAQ later puts the theoretical time at about 1.7 hours if you figure 90% charging efficiency.

The inverter charger weighs about 10.1 pounds. LiTime does not list the battery weight, but I weighted it after I took it out of the packaging and it was about 52 pounds. With the floor stand, the two modules stood up together are 20.47 inches wide, 30.71 inches tall, and 3.94 inches deep. It runs at about 40 decibels (which is very quiet) and switches over to battery in 10 milliseconds or less. It has a touchscreen, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5.0, and the LiTime app, plus a time-of-use mode so you can charge off-peak.

Industry observers note that the price on LiTime’s site is $1,099.99, shown as $100 off. US preorders opened October 20, 2026, and when I checked, estimated delivery was November 24 to 27.

Recent findings suggest that liTime calls this “space-based” home backup. Instead of trying to power the whole house, you protect one room, in this case the kitchen. You plug the system into a wall outlet and plug the fridge into the K1. No electrician and no panel work. LiTime estimates about 24 hours of backup on a large side-by-side refrigerator (while I got a bit more than that in my testing) that uses about 2 kilowatt-hours a day, or about 99 hours with four batteries if the fridge is the only load. Depending on the load, it can also run a microwave, an air fryer, a toaster, or a coffee maker for a basic meal. Just don’t try to run them all at once. You can run two smaller loads at once, but a large load like a microwave or air fryer needs to be run by itself (you can keep your refrigerator plugged in too). LiTime says to allow for compressor startup if you also want to run one of those at the same time.

You can wall-mount it, stand it on the floor, or lean it against a wall, with the two modules together or apart. It comes with mounting hardware and two connection cables, 0.25 meters and 1.5 meters (about 10 inches and 5 feet). The battery housing is steel, and LiTime says the metal finish is meant to suit a kitchen. The inverter is rated IP20, so it stays indoors. LiTime says separating the inverter from the battery cuts down on heat transfer, which they claim helps the battery last longer. I have not measured that.

According to recent reports, for a plug & play system, this is a new product category. There have been portable generators available for years that could be used for camping or appliance backup, but having a product tailored to a specific room is a new concept. The comparison they offer is this one-room approach versus a whole-house battery system, the kind that usually needs panel work and that will cost you about 10 times as much.

You can use this for camping or travel, but it isn’t built for it. With split modules, wall-mount hardware, only two AC outlets, and no USB ports, this is built for a permanent kitchen install, not something you toss in the car for a weekend trip.

It has been revealed that I used my old Kill-A-Watt meter to have an independent measure of the draw on the battery from the refrigerator. During the test, I opened the refrigerator less than I normally would, but still opened it about 10 times.

Next I wanted to test it with my small kitchen appliances. First, one at a time; then, several at once. It is rated at 2000 watts continuous, but it should be able to surge up to 4000 watts for 1 second.

Industry observers note that notice that it pulls 2510 watts from the battery, but the load is only 2290 watts. Where did the other 220 watts go? That must be used by the inverter to convert DC to AC.

According to recent reports, after 35 years of Tampa storm seasons, I’ve learned that the fridge is usually the first thing you worry about when the power goes out. The LiTime Lares K1 is built for exactly that. In my testing it kept our large side-by-side GE refrigerator running for almost 26 hours on one battery, a bit longer than LiTime’s own estimate of 24 hours. It then shut off cleanly to protect the appliance. Recharging from the wall took about 3 hours, with 80% back in about 2 hours.

Industry observers note that it also handled my small kitchen appliances well. The air fryer, coffee maker, and refrigerator ran together at about 2,200 watts, a little over the rated 2,000. When I added the toaster to push it past its limits, it briefly put out about 3,140 watts and then dropped back to about 2,130 watts without shutting down. The app also showed about 220 watts lost in converting battery power to AC, which is worth keeping in mind when you estimate runtime.

It does have limits. There are only two outlets, no USB ports, and the battery weighs about 52 pounds, so this is a permanent kitchen install, not a camping generator. Adding batteries gives you more runtime, but not more output.

In a recent development, at $1,099.99, with no electrician or panel work needed and a 5-year battery warranty, the Lares K1 is an affordable way to protect your food and still cook a basic meal during an outage. It costs about a tenth of what a whole-house battery would. If kitchen backup is what you care about most, it’s well worth a look.

#110924. Steel solar panel frames hit the mainstream

Steel solar panel frames hit the mainstream

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1347 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Solarpowerworldonline

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Steel is considered the backbone of the American economy, critical for both national and economic security.
  • Recent findings suggest that A factory worker places a section of steel solar panel frames on a pallet in Welser Profile’s plant in Valley City, Ohio.
  • Industry observers note that roll-form steel company Welser Profile began manufacturing Nextpower’s NX CoreFrame steel panel frames earlier this year at its facility in Valley City, Ohio, just 30 miles outside Cleveland, and Solar Power World was invited to view production of its first major orders before adding another line fully dedicated to the solar component before the end of the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steel is considered the backbone of the American economy, critical for both national and economic security. It’s also the backbone of solar power construction, found commonly in the racking and mounting structures tilting solar panels toward the sun. And now, after years of tests and trials, an Ohio factory is roll-forming steel for a solar product that could use a stronger backbone — the solar panel.

Recent findings suggest that A factory worker places a section of steel solar panel frames on a pallet in Welser Profile’s plant in Valley City, Ohio. Credit: Nextpower.

Industry observers note that roll-form steel company Welser Profile began manufacturing Nextpower’s NX CoreFrame steel panel frames earlier this year at its facility in Valley City, Ohio, just 30 miles outside Cleveland, and Solar Power World was invited to view production of its first major orders before adding another line fully dedicated to the solar component before the end of the year. Module frame company Origami Solar originally had the idea that swapping aluminum frames with steel would not only save the solar industry money and cut back on carbon emissions, it would also provide more physical support to bigger and heavier solar panels.

Welser, an Austrian firm with origins dating back to the 1660s, is a leader in roll-form steel profiles typically only seen in aluminum extrusions and helped produce a steel frame that’s easy for panel manufacturers to assemble and contractors to handle.

“What’s special about Welser Profile is we pre-notch features in the material before it gets formed,” stated Bill Johnson, North America CEO of Welser Profile. “Everything about the solar industry is about how do we make it more efficient, cheaper, faster, better? You do that by all these little details to add value farther up the stream that minimizes labor, install cost. Our hole patterns and other features allow operators to snap things together, not bolt or weld things. Everyone is looking at how to make this work in a Lego setup, not a high-intense labor workforce installing all these panels.”.

Welser is helping bring the Origami Solar idea to life, but the new owner of the tech, Nextpower, is delivering steel frames to the masses. Nextpower, a steel expert through its experience in producing tracking and mounting systems, acquired Origami in 2025 and will use its existing network of steel partners to convince more PV project developers to consider an alternative to aluminum.

According to recent reports, “Nextpower has launched over 30 manufacturing facilities in the U.S. since 2020. Nextpower buys over 700,000 short tons of primary U.S. steel annually, which is more than a small car company,” said Jenya Meydbray, VP and general manager of Nextpower’s steel frames business. “Nextpower has had [the steel frame] for one year, building on the years of Origami’s engineering with Welser’s support. What we’re doing today is launching into high-scale, high-volume production here in Ohio.”.

The solar industry defaulted to aluminum panel frames because the material is lightweight, easy to handle and less susceptible to corrosion. But as the solar industry matured, more environmental and practical concerns became associated with the metal. Aluminum production on average has a five-times larger carbon footprint than steel production, a difficult point to ignore in the inherently green solar industry. Solar panels have also gotten larger in surface area and use less glass to cut weight. Aluminum might no longer be the ideal material to physically support these “massive, floppy modules.”.

A steel coil feeds into a roll-forming machine producing solar panel frames. Credit: Nextpower.

“Steel provides a far better structural support for the [panel] than aluminum does. That was the initial observation that the Origami founders made,” Meydbray said. “They landed on this specific [roll-form] profile. Roll-forming is a precision process. We’re making millions of sticks of solar panel frames a month, and all of them have to be within sub-millimeter of precision across the full length. Welser is 100 years older than America, so Welser is definitely the most experienced in this art form of steel roll-forming.”.

Welser set up North American operations in 2018 after acquiring an automotive roll-form operation in Valley City. The tech giant established a second location in the same industrial park to accommodate its growing client base in the solar, storage and energy industries.

Sources indicate that welser was one of the first roll-form partners to validate Magnelis — a zinc magnesium coating that has “self-healing” properties is capable of lasting 25 years in the field — and found it a great steel coating for solar energy applications. It’s one of the features of NX CoreFrame, Nextpower’s steel solar module frame.

“Coming up with a new coating on steel, you don’t just throw it on the steel and sell it to the market. You have to trial it, validate it, make sure it works,” Johnson remarked. “Raw zinc — the coating has to be too thick for the longevity that the solar industry needs. Magnelis can go much lighter coating and still produce the same salt spray, same longevity, and it’s cheaper, faster, smarter.”.

Wesler is the latest high-volume production facility for NX CoreFrame, and Nextpower plans to reach 6.5 GW of annual production through additional manufacturing partners across the country.

With an established steel frame design, the product just needs to find a place on panel manufacturer’s production lines. Origami Solar had been signing supply agreements with U.S. panel assemblers, an activity that has only increased with the Nextpower transition. Meydbray remarked the pitch for a domestic supply chain has become more attractive, especially with Nextpower’s established regional steel manufacturing network.

A machine treats steel coil as it travels along a factory line. Credit: Nextpower.

According to recent reports, “Steel strengthens the supply chain of domestic manufacturing facilities. When frames are bought overseas, they spend five, six weeks on the water before they actually arrive to the factory. [Panel companies] have about 2,000 pallets of frames in inventory when they source from overseas,” he noted. “We’re able to provide actual just-in-time delivery to our factory clients. We can make deliveries every 48 hours. [They can save room] where they used to have pallets stacked up. There’s also the working capital of having stuff sit on the water for six weeks. Solar panel manufacturing is not a high-margin business, and working capital management is critical.”.

Nextpower has inked supply agreements with many multi-gigawatt panel manufacturers in the United States, including Jinko, T1 and Thornova.

Industry observers note that “This integration of Nextpower steel frames allows us to deliver high-performance modules tailored to the evolving U.S. market,” mentioned Andrea Bodenhagen, global marketing director at Thornova Solar, which is establishing domestic solar cell manufacturing in Oklahoma. “By incorporating U.S.-made steel frames, we strengthen supply chain resilience while helping our customers maximize domestic content and improve project economics.”.

With bonus incentives from the investment tax credit still in play when solar projects use domestic products, an American-made steel frame can make all the difference.

Sources indicate that “When we see projects that have 100% domestic content on the tracker, we know that’s a perfect candidate for steel frames,” Meydbray stated. “Steel frames get 6% domestic content credit. It’s the second cheapest percent after the tracker. A domestically made solar cell is a lot more expensive than an imported solar cell. The frame is the second-most cost-effective way to buy percentage points.”.

The NX CoreFrame is universal and can be used with any brand’s mounting or tracking system, but there are advantages when the project can be designed more cohesively through one supplier. Nextpower has spent the last year expanding beyond mounting systems, now offering inverter, electrical balance of system and panel products.

Industry observers note that “[Nextpower] is ambitious, but it’s not arrogant. It prioritizes the customer relationships it’s built over the years. We spent time with our customers asking where their pain points are and expanded the business accordingly …  the firm that makes the thing the solar panel is mounted to is the same company that makes the frame that’s being mounted,” Meydbray said.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peugeot might have major racing victories in three different centuries, but that heritage wasn't enough to save its Le Mans Hypercar program.
  • Stellantis stated it intends to "refocus its motorsport activities and resources on customer racing and high-performance vehicle development." Amid the tech giant's dire financial situation, CEO Antonio Filosa set a goal early this year of $6.6 billion in cost savings by 2028.
  • Recent findings suggest that there were two silver linings to Stellantis' decision.

Peugeot might have major racing victories in three different centuries, but that heritage wasn't enough to save its Le Mans Hypercar program. Stellantis unveiled on Monday that it's pulling the plug on all its factory motorsports programs, confirming last week's reports. The automotive giant won't fully shutter the motorsport division, hoping to still generate revenue from customer racing. The only projects to avoid the axe were its North American subsidiary's revived NASCAR efforts under the Dodge and Ram brands.

Stellantis stated it intends to "refocus its motorsport activities and resources on customer racing and high-performance vehicle development." Amid the tech giant's dire financial situation, CEO Antonio Filosa set a goal early this year of $6.6 billion in cost savings by 2028. The decision was sudden for the programs. Peugeot planned to compete with an updated 9X8 in next year's FIA World Endurance Championship and had already begun testing the upcoming prototype. With Alpine's previously announced departure, this means there will be no French manufacturer in the top class of the 2027 24 Hours of Le Mans.

Recent findings suggest that there were two silver linings to Stellantis' decision. First, the organization will be continuing its customer racing programs. Second, the company's two Formula E teams will be allowed to contest the upcoming season. Citroën and Opel collaborated in developing newly introduced cars for the debut Gen4 campaign. These 800-horsepower machines will get a single season in the sun (or rain) before getting sent to the scrap heap. It's a similar situation to what happened to Lancia's WRC2 program, with the Ypsilon Rally2 HF Integrale running its maiden season this year before Stellantis pulled the plug.

Industry observers note that as much as some auto executives champion the "win on Sunday, sell on Monday" mentality, the exposure of being in a motorsport series only truly exists if you're competing in the front half of the field. Using Formula 1 as an example, Aston Martin and Cadillac might as well not exist to TV cameras unless their cars crash or get lapped by the leaders. Saving the Peugeot 9X8 program would be a hard sell for anyone because LMH went five years without winning a WEC race or finishing a Le Mans podium.

  • A coastal flood advisory has been issued for the Pacific Northwest and parts of Northern California, and there's at the moment a nor'easter storm that looks like it will bring heavy rains, winds, and coastal flooding to the entire East Coast over the course of Wednesday and Thursday.
  • According to recent reports, the National Weather Service determined that the nor'easter storm strengthening off the southeastern coast could undergo rapid cyclogenesis and become a bomb cyclone by Thanksgiving day.

The weeks surrounding the Thanksgiving holiday are some of the busiest travel days of the year in the United States. This year, AAA projects that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday November 24 and Monday, November 30, and it projects that 72.8 million of those Americans will be making that drive by car. That's actually a slight drop from last year's result of 73.1 million travelers, but AAA states travelers in major metropolitan areas could still expect to see more than double the normal traffic congestion. We think that may even be a conservative estimate, given that weather forecasts across the country tell a stormy story.

A coastal flood advisory has been issued for the Pacific Northwest and parts of Northern California, and there's at the moment a nor'easter storm that looks like it will bring heavy rains, winds, and coastal flooding to the entire East Coast over the course of Wednesday and Thursday. The mayor of San Francisco even posted a video to social media urging people to avoid unnecessary travel, saying, "If you don't need to, please don't travel into the city. We always want visitors, but these are special circumstances." We got all your wet weather driving tips to help folks prepare for the Super El Niño a few months ago, so feel free to revisit that if you can't avoid driving in stormy conditions.

According to recent reports, the National Weather Service determined that the nor'easter storm strengthening off the southeastern coast could undergo rapid cyclogenesis and become a bomb cyclone by Thanksgiving day. It's also expected to bring powerful winds with gusts of over 50 mph along the coast and 40 mph inland. The most significant effects are expected to impact the mid-Atlantic and Northeast, so be sure to check the weather forecast in your area before making your elderly grandparents brave treacherous roads.

Industry observers note that west Coast travelers should be aware of the impact of potentially record-high king tides as well as a storm that's expected to bring rain, high-elevation snow, and dense fog from San Francisco all the way up the coast to Southern Washington. This king tide is expected to amplify the already elevated sea levels that have been affecting the West Coast thanks to the Super El Niño's higher water temperatures, potentially causing a surge of more than eight feet in San Francisco Bay. Waves are also expected to become dangerously large, reaching sizes of 20 to 30 feet on Wednesday. Federal experts say San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (OAK), two of the largest airports in California's populous Bay Area, will flood this week from the huge tides. If you've been looking for an excuse to avoid the holiday chaos and stay home to play more GTA, just blame the weather forecast and order takeout.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as the wind energy industry matures, operators and service providers are increasingly focused on maximizing turbine availability while controlling long-term maintenance costs. Although major drivetrain components often receive the spotlight, one overlooked system can have an outsized impact on turbine reliability and performance: gearbox oil cooling.

Heat exchangers play a critical role in maintaining proper oil temperature and viscosity within wind turbine gearboxes. When cooling systems become clogged with airborne debris, dust, or organic material, oil temperatures rise, lubrication performance declines, and component stress increases. Over time, these conditions can contribute to reduced gearbox efficiency, elevated maintenance demands, and avoidable downtime.

Recent findings suggest that “Wind operators today are balancing increasing performance expectations with the realities of aging fleets and rising maintenance costs. Technologies that improve cooling efficiency and reduce service exposure can have a meaningful impact on long-term turbine reliability and operational profitability,” according to Mike Erickson, HYDAC’s Market Manager for the Wind Industry.

Traditional “panel cut” heat exchanger designs have long been susceptible to clogging due to their tightly packed fin structures. In many wind environments — particularly agricultural, dusty, or high-pollen regions — debris accumulation can severely restrict airflow. Oil leaks can further compound the issue by trapping contaminants within the exchanger core, making cleaning more difficult and labor intensive.

This operational challenge has driven the need for more resilient cooling technologies designed specifically for real-world wind farm conditions.

HYDAC’s latest “Square Wave” heat exchanger design represents a significant advancement in addressing these reliability concerns. Engineered to allow debris to pass more freely through the exchanger fins, the design minimizes clogging while improving cooling efficiency under demanding operating conditions.

The importance of effective cooling cannot be overstated. Wind turbine gearbox oil typically operates within an optimal temperature range of approximately 45°C to 65°C. Even modest temperature increases can significantly impact oil viscosity. According to field data, a 12°C rise in oil temperature can reduce viscosity by nearly 28 percent — affecting lubrication quality and accelerating wear on critical drivetrain components.

Sources indicate that field trials have demonstrated measurable operational benefits from the Square Wave design. During a one-year trial on GE 1.x turbines, the upgraded exchanger consistently reduced clogging and lowered maintenance requirements compared to traditional panel cut cores. Operators reported reduced up-tower cleaning time and fewer temperature-related cooling faults.

Recent findings suggest that field validation across multiple turbine platforms has further reinforced the operational advantages of the Square Wave design. In one case study involving legacy 1 MW-class turbines operating in the Pacific Northwest, a major renewable energy operator installed pilot sets of Square Wave heat exchangers as part of a cooling performance evaluation. Installation teams reported the upgraded exchangers integrated seamlessly into the existing platform with no retrofit complications.

Sources indicate that after initial operating data demonstrated improved cooling consistency, the operator expanded the evaluation program with additional units. Long-term SCADA analysis later demonstrated turbines equipped with Square Wave technology operate approximately 20 to 25 percent cooler than comparable turbines using conventional heat exchanger designs under similar operating conditions. The data also highlighted another crucial advantage: the Square Wave cores continued to maintain airflow and cooling efficiency in debris-heavy environments where traditional exchanger designs became increasingly restricted over time.

The successful deployment also generated interest from additional wind service organizations seeking retrofit-ready cooling upgrades that could improve turbine reliability while reducing maintenance burdens across aging fleets.

“What operators are increasingly recognizing is that small improvements in thermal management can create meaningful gains in turbine reliability, maintenance efficiency, and long-term asset performance,” said Erickson. “The field data we’re seeing continues to validate the value of designing cooling systems specifically for real-world wind operating environments.”.

Industry observers note that more recently, long-term SCADA data from Mitsubishi platforms further validated the technology’s performance. After two years of operation, turbines equipped with Square Wave heat exchangers operated approximately 19 to 25 percent cooler than reference turbines using standard exchanger designs under comparable operating conditions.

For wind asset owners and service providers, the implications are substantial: Improved thermal management supports healthier oil viscosity, more stable gearbox operation, and potentially longer component life. At the same time, reduced cleaning frequency and fewer cooling-related service events translate directly into lower operational expenditures and increased turbine availability.

As the industry continues to prioritize lifecycle optimization and energy production efficiency, innovative subsystem upgrades such as advanced heat exchanger technology are becoming increasingly valuable. Rather than waiting for costly failures or performance degradation, operators are seeking practical retrofit solutions that improve reliability without requiring major system redesigns.

According to recent reports, “Effective thermal management is critical to protecting gearbox health and maintaining oil performance over time. By addressing one of the most common causes of cooling degradation — debris accumulation — operators can improve uptime while reducing unnecessary maintenance interventions,” said HYDAC’s Erickson.

For wind stakeholders evaluating ways to improve gearbox reliability, reduce maintenance exposure, and enhance turbine performance, cooling system optimization deserves greater attention. Proven retrofit technologies like advanced heat exchanger designs can offer a practical path toward improved uptime and operational efficiency without requiring major system overhauls.

In a recent development, as fleets age and performance expectations continue to rise, collaboration between operators, service providers, and technology partners will be essential to building more resilient wind assets for the future. Now is the time to evaluate whether existing cooling systems are supporting — or limiting — long-term turbine reliability goals.

“HYDAC’s goal is to help wind owners and service providers solve practical operational challenges in ways that create long-term value across the entire asset lifecycle. Innovations like the Square Wave heat exchanger are designed to improve reliability, simplify maintenance, and support greater energy production over time.”.

Don’t let cooling system limitations impact turbine performance.

90 Latest Vehicle Models Were Just Introduced in Colombia’s Largest Automotive Exhibition. 55 Were Electric.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2208 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The last two weeks, the future was on display in Bogota’s Automobile Hall.
  • This Hall is Colombia’s largest and most important Automotive Exhibition, and since 2023 (17th edition, held after a hiatus of 5 years), it has heralded the unstoppable tide of EVs progressively taking over the national market.
  • Sources indicate that EVs have been gaining ground since, with more of them arriving every year, and in the latest iteration of the Automobile Hall, we’ve reached a point of no return: EVs make up a majority of the newly declared models arriving in the country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The last two weeks, the future was on display in Bogota’s Automobile Hall.

This Hall is Colombia’s largest and most important Automotive Exhibition, and since 2023 (17th edition, held after a hiatus of 5 years), it has heralded the unstoppable tide of EVs progressively taking over the national market. Back then, despite EVs making up less than 3% of the market, EVs were already present and relevant in the Automobile Hall, with the Changan Lumin being a particularly bright star.

Sources indicate that EVs have been gaining ground since, with more of them arriving every year, and in the latest iteration of the Automobile Hall, we’ve reached a point of no return: EVs make up a majority of the newly declared models arriving in the country. Or to be specific: out of 90 arrivals, EVs account for 55!

32 brands brought fresh electric or plug-in hybrid cars to showcase in Bogota’s Automobile Hall. Even though most of them (unsurprisingly) are from China, we still find presences from 7 European and 2 Japanese brands here — all will be listed at the end of this article with their respective models.

Most of these models arrive at very competitive pricing, many times undercutting their direct gasoline and diesel competition, and with ever-improving specs — by reasonable standards, most of these cars should be able to make at least 350 km on Colombian roads, making them quite appealing options even for people who travel regularly.

Colombia’s EV market share has been growing in 2026, reaching 20% — or almost — every month since March. But with this EV avalanche (or EV-lanche), I think it’s inevitable that we will see that number go up in the months to come — though how fast exactly, I leave to you to debate.

And no, you were not the only ones to notice that there are exactly zero (0) arrivals from US brands. Tesla was of course present, but with nothing new (though they did present the Cybercab at a later date than I attended), other than Tesla, US brands are either too small or too focused on gas-guzzlers to bother even trying to compete.

Note: all prices mentioned here include taxes, but registration and insurance may not be included.

I will start with the non-Chinese EVs, because, well, they’re fewer.

The most notable model here, by far, is the Renault 4 e-Tech. People outside this country probably don’t know that the Renault 4 was built here for 22 years, becoming the most affordable car for decades and a symbol of the Colombian middle class. Nicknamed the “Colombian Car” and the “Loyal Friend,” the Renault 4 has a place in the hearth of most Colombians, and, as such, the R4 e-Tech was one of the most visited cars in the entire exhibition.

According to recent reports, because of this, it’s certain that the car will have some buyers. But at 100 million COP (€26,000, $28,500), it’s a hard sell, particularly when the hatchback segment has stabilized somewhere around $20,000 for Chinese models. Nostalgia has a price for sure, but not that many people will be willing to pay $8,500 for it.

The BMW iX3 was also present in the hall, and I must admit it’s a very compelling and impressive car, but at 300 million COP ($85,400), there are not a lot of buyers that will be interested.

From the European side, other than Renault and BMW, we have the Cupra Terramar and the Mini Cooper SE Paul Smith Edition, both around 160 million COP (€41,700, $45,500). So, quite expensive for their segments, even though I find the Terramar a very beautiful car. The Porsche Cayenne is of course expensive beyond anything seen prior, and the Volvo EX60 has not unveiled pricing yet. As for Stellantis, it’s betting on its two vans, somewhat expensive but still viable, and it has the Opel Crossland EV, which has been on the market for a while but is now discounted to 90 million COP (€23,400, $25,600), meaning it’s one of the most competitive non-Chinese EVs available.

Regarding the Japanese, the Toyota BZ4X (already present) and the RAV4 PHEV (just arriving) are of course important players, but at 220 million and 270 million COP respectively ($62,600 and $76,800), they won’t sell more than a trickle of units. The Nissan Frontier Pro has the same price as the BZ4X, and, to be fair, I didn’t even notice it was available until I left the Hall.

Paradoxically, the most competitive non-Chinese EVs all come from a brand with zero arrivals: Kia. With its EV2 starting at 90 million COP and its EV3 at 120 million COP ($23,400 and $34,100), Kia has the closest prices to any Chinese competitor and can at least rely on the brand’s popularity to keep some of the market.

With that out of the way, let’s look at the Chinese arrivals, or at least some of them, as there are too many to mention.

Industry observers note that you can see the full list of models at the end of the article. Here I will focus on those I think will make the most impact in the market.

First, one of my favorite EVs: the all-mighty Chery ICaur V23. In a previous article I mentioned how surprising its low range was … but I must admit I judged it rashly. I mean, that thing is huge. I really expected it to be much smaller, and thus I understand why it can barely edge a 360 km range (WLTP) despite a sizeable 81 kWh battery. When you’re built like a small tank, you can expect to get the range of a small tank, no surprises here.

But the great selling point for this car is its price: 85 million COP for the 4×2 version and 105 million COP for the 4×4 version ($24,100 and $29,900). We’re talking a fully off-road capable SUV for the same or less than a Renault 4 or a Corolla. Truly impressive, and an example of EV innovation in segments that many other OEMs have not dared enter, assuming they are lost to the ICEV competition.

BYD also surprised by bringing a latest Sealion RWD, armed with a 70 kWh battery and aimed directly against the Model Y. At 115 million COP ($32,700), this car is $1,500 cheaper than the Model Y RWD while having a larger battery and better range. It seems the Chinese giant wants to start getting back some market share a year after the US brand took the market by storm. Better late than never I guess.

BYD is also bringing the EREV Leopard 7 under its own brand (BYD Ti7), but at 225 million COP ($64,000), it will certainly not be a best seller, even though it will probably give the likes of Toyota and Land Rover a run for their money.

In a recent development, now, my dear readers, I hope you will forgive me here, but even though I actually went to the Hall to take a look to the XPeng Mona L03 specifically, it seems I got distracted by the robot and the drone-licopter, and thus this is the picture you’re getting … because I forgot to take one of the L03. Regardless, the XPeng L03 is also pointing directly at Tesla, arriving at 115 million COP ($32,700), the same price of the entry-level Model 3, except the L03 provides full self-driving capabilities for this price, to the extent that XPeng can provide that of course. This car (available in BEV and PHEV versions) and the BYD Sealion are poised to bring a significant challenge not only to Tesla, but to the entire ICEV ecosystem, which is having evermore competition in its bread-and-butter segments by the month.

There are currently 6 subcompact entry-level SUVs fighting in the 80-to-95 million COP segment: the Chery Omoda E5, the MG S5, the Dongfeng Vigo, the Faw Bestune Joy, the Changan Nevo Q05, and the Ora 5.

I chose the Ora 5 to represent the segment because it offers the largest battery (58kWh, vs 50kWh for all the others) and, as of the Automobile Hall, the lowest price for the entry-level version, at only 73 million COP (USD $20.800). This is a true bargain, making it the cheapest available SUV of any powertrain by quite some distance, and a very compelling option for budget-oriented buyers. It remains to be seen if this price will remain after the Hall.

Sources indicate that going by specs alone, I believe the JMEV GSX to be the best value-for-money vehicle currently available in the Colombian market. This SUV boasts an impressive 70 kWh battery with 500 km WLTP range for a mere 90 million COP ($25,600). The only thing against it is that JMEV (JMC) is quite a small brand and has not gained traction in this market, or in any other that I know of.

Industry observers note that in Colombia, this minicar has taken the place that belonged to the Wuling Hongguang in China, and more recently belongs to the Chery QQ Ice Cream — that of a (barely) highway-capable minicar that may seat four, or two plus your groceries, but that will fit in any spot and can be parked wherever you may find a square meter available. Available with a brand new 18.1 kWh battery, the Faw Xiaoma 2.0 remains the most affordable “true” car in Colombia at 40 million COP ($11,400).

It’s worth noting that Faw has failed to gain traction in the Colombian market, and it clearly wanted to change that in this Hall, as it brought an entire armada, with its N09 Sedan available for 100 million COP ($28,300) as its flagship car.

Aside from minicars (like the Xiaoma above), the Dongfeng Box deserves a mention for being the cheapest car in the hatchback segment at 65 million COP ($18,500). With its 42 kWh battery, it can reasonably travel long distance with the current infrastructure. I’ve ridden in both this car and the Geely EX2, and, frankly, the EX2 has a higher quality feel, but this one is slightly cheaper, and no doubt this will bring some buyers.

At a price of only 75 million COP ($21,350), the Foton e-Wonder mini-truck provides full price parity with diesel versions and opens the possibility of electrification for the owners of smaller companies. At 1-ton carrying capacity, it’s a very compelling vehicle, even if its 40 kWh battery remains limited for long-distance operations.

Of course, this list would not be complete without the most affordable “real” car here (so, not minicars included, sorry Xiaoma!). The Jac E10X is a city-car available for 60 million COP ($17,000), and even though it looks good and has decent quality, it has never sold well because JAC is not a very popular brand, and because its 30 kWh battery lacks capacity for making even medium-distance trips without having at least some range anxiety.

Recent findings suggest that well, this is it. My apologies for the fans of Arcfox and Leapmotor — both are very important brands arriving in the country, but Arcfox lacks recognition and prices are a bit over the competition (they are a luxury brand, but that may not convince people who don’t already know them) and Leapmotor only brought EREVs, and as you may have seen, I focused on BEVs in the very long Chinese list.

My conclusions are probably quite predictable. China is leading and by quite an advantage, the Koreans are not too far behind, the Europeans are trying to make a comeback, the Japanese are making a symbolic (but useless) stand, and the Americans — other than Tesla — didn’t even bother to show up.

Industry observers note that it’s hard to believe only three years have passed since Bogota’s Automobile Hall of 2023, when the Changan Lumin was the star and when we were celebrating going over 2% market share. Back then, EVs were still expensive, charging infrastructure was much more limited, and the mainstream was firmly on the pure-combustion side, with hybrids making some inroads.

Now, after the EV-lanche we’re seeing, it seems that EVs are now fully in the mainstream, with lower prices and better specs than ever before. EV sales will keep growing fast, and I expect the market to tilt even more to the side of zero-emissions transportation in the coming months. 30% BEV market share is now well within sight.

For those of you who want to look at the full list of arrivals, here it is below. BEVs are in bold, PHEVs and EREVs are in regular.

Arcfox T5, T1, S5; Avatr 11, 7; BAIC X55; BYD Sealion RWD, Ti7 (Leopard 7), Atto 8; Deepal S09; Denza Z9 GT, B5; Dongfeng 7, 8; Farizon V7E, F3E; Faw Xiaoma 2.0, Joyee N09, Joyee S08; Foton E-Tunland; GAC Aion UT 2027, S7; Geely Monjaro EM-I, Starray EM-R; GWM Tank 700, ICaur V23, V27; IM IM6; Jetour G700, T2; JMEV GSX; Leapmotor B10, C10; Lynk & Co 2, 1, 8, 900; MHero II; Rox Motor 1; Xpeng L03, L03; Zeekr 007GT, 001FR, 9X.

BMW iX3, iX5, i7; Cupra Terramar; Mini Cooper SE Paul Smith; Peugeot E-Partner, Peugeot E-Expert; Porsche Cayenne; Renault R4 E-Tech; Volvo EX60.

Nissan Frontier Pro, Toyota RAV4.

#110914. 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda For Sale With 58,000 Miles Shown Is Racing Royalty With A Wild History

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (800 w)

1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda For Sale With 58,000 Miles Shown Is Racing Royalty With A Wild History

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that special is subjective — even when it comes to cars.
  • In a recent development, every once in a great while, one of these special Mopar muscle cars comes up for sale.
  • It has been revealed that you might not expect a 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda to rack up race wins in France, but this 'Cuda did just that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that special is subjective — even when it comes to cars. A car that is special to you might just be junk to somebody else. Sorry to burst your bubble, but not every car can count itself among the unicorns and truly special automotive special editions. Then again, other cars are special, full stop. Cars with the sort of presence that makes the little hairs on the back of your neck stand at attention. Understandably, most of us don't often get to see such cars, like the Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda. Big V8 power and an even bigger personality promptly established the short-lived E-Body Hemi 'Cuda as a muscle car mainstay.

In a recent development, every once in a great while, one of these special Mopar muscle cars comes up for sale. But seldom does one with this sort of record head to the auction block. This is not a Hollywood car, nor was it celebrity-owned. No, this 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda has a racing rap sheet longer than your arm, teeming with victories and championship wins. Better yet, the 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8-powered racing legend racked up its impressive record as a primary factory-backed race car for Ecurie Chrysler in France, of all places. This is one well-traveled 'Cuda. Now, the esteemed asphalt-kicking American ambassador and its 58,000-mile odometer are back in the U.S. of A. and up for grabs courtesy of Bring a Trailer.

It has been revealed that you might not expect a 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda to rack up race wins in France, but this 'Cuda did just that. Henri Chemin, the Chrysler France competition director at the time, drove the car in many Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) and Fédération Française du Sport Automobile (FFSA) events. Chemin managed nine victories in 1970, 16 wins in 1971, and seven victories in 1972. Jean-François Mas took the wheel in 1973, winning 12 times in 1973. This Hemi 'Cuda's last recorded victory was the handiwork of Jean-Claude Géral, who drove the muscle car to victory at the 1974 hillclimb event in Charnizay. All said and done, the 'Cuda claimed 45 Group 1 wins and three FIA championships between 1970 and 1974.

Sources indicate that so, what state is the car in today? For starters, the restored-and-retired racer packs a 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8. That Hemi replaced the 'Cuda's original mill during the 1971 season. Should the next owner want to set up a display, the sale includes the original engine block, as well as extensive documentation, photos, a Simca en Compétition racing book, and Chemin's press clippings. A Hurst pistol-grip shifter commands the 'Cuda's four-speed manual transmission, while a Shaker hood and air dam help the old Mopar look the part.

In keeping with its racing DNA, the old Plymouth features a roll cage, Simpson harnesses, and a white-and-blue racing livery. Other features include 15" Rally wheels in a complementary white hue, body-colored bumpers, front disc brakes, a wood-rimmed steering wheel, an ATL fuel cell, and a dual exhaust system with Flowmaster mufflers.

We don't have to tell you that racing is dangerous — for both driver and machine. Duh, right? Well, at the Brides–Méribel hillclimb event in 1970, the Ecurie Chrysler Hemi 'Cuda met with a motorsport disaster of its own. Piloted by Chemin, the 'Cuda's power steering failed, causing the car to crash into a ravine. The crash was as bad as it sounds. Ecurie Chrysler deemed the Plymouth's body shell beyond repair. So, the racing team's engineers and mechanics salvaged everything they could, including the original engine, much of the drivetrain, the gauges, and the seats. They then transplanted it all into a replacement E-body from a 440 Six-Pack 'Cuda that Chemin had brought into France with the original factory-backed car.

Want this one? You're going to pay for it. As of this writing, the high bid for the Ex-Ecurie Chrysler France 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda is $110,000. Now, stock and well-preserved Hemi 'Cudas routinely net six-figure sums when they go up for sale. Don't believe it? This 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda with 31,300 miles that we reported on last month sold for $176,000 on Mecum. Add a factory convertible configuration into the mix, and a third-gen Hemi 'Cuda has the potential to cross the block for seven figures. After all, just 12 factory rag-top Hemi 'Cudas rolled off the line as 1971 models, making the classic Plymouth a 'Holy Grail' of muscle cars.

There's plenty of space for this motorsport Mopar to sell for big bucks. We just hope someone buys this tenured racing machine and lets it off its leash from time to time. It would be a shame for this one to spend too much time locked away from view with an odometer reading under 60,000 miles.

Latest Update: Slate Thinks 205 Miles Is More Than Enough Range

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yes, with a starting price of $26,400, including destination, the two-door pickup truck it's selling is cheap compared to the competition, but it also lacks basic features like power windows and a radio at that price.
  • In a recent development, it makes sense why the Slate has such a shoddy range, even compared to its competition.
  • Recent findings suggest that still, Slate feels 205 miles is really all the average American needs from a vehicle like its truck, the cheapest EV and pickup for sale in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Slate Auto is in a strange spot. Yes, with a starting price of $26,400, including destination, the two-door pickup truck it's selling is cheap compared to the competition, but it also lacks basic features like power windows and a radio at that price. With options that'll make the truck more livable for everyday use, prices will quickly climb. No matter which options they choose, they'll still be saddled with the same 205 miles of range. Even though that's quite meager by today's standards, Slate feels that's more than enough to win over customers.

In a recent development, it makes sense why the Slate has such a shoddy range, even compared to its competition. The battery is the single most expensive part of an electric vehicle, so an automaker looking to make a cheap EV will use a smaller battery. There's a view that Slate's approach could work for folks who are already comfortable with EVs, but it might not translate for those more accustomed to what gas-powered vehicles offer, according to Automotive News. There's also the glitch that similarly priced rivals will offer more range on base models, and they usually have the option of extended-range batteries.

Recent findings suggest that still, Slate feels 205 miles is really all the average American needs from a vehicle like its truck, the cheapest EV and pickup for sale in the U.S. To be fair, it's also the smallest pickup in the U.S. — about two feet shorter than a Ford Maverick. In a marketing email sent earlier this month, Slate noted 205 miles is "more than [many people] need each day." That's sort of fair, because according to a 2024 survey done by AAA, the average American drives about 31 miles per day, meaning that from full to empty, you'd only need to charge the Slate about once a week. Of course, no one actually drives like that, and the range will never actually be 205 miles, but we can't really account for that.

Slate isn't the only firm offering an EV with less-than-stellar range. The Kia EV3 compact crossover, which starts at $31,385, comes as standard with 221 miles of range. While the starting prices are far different, the EV3 comes with a lot more from the get-go. To get the Slate to a comparable place, you've got to add a bed kit that brings in seats and a roof — giving the Slate "crossover" a $31,400 base price, according to AutoNews. It'll still be missing plenty of other things at that price, like a radio and electric windows.

Recent findings suggest that in any case, Kia doesn't expect this low-range EV3 to be a major seller — capturing just 3 to 5% of its sales. The higher Wind trim, with its 321 miles of range and $36,485 starting price, is expected to be the volume seller with about 60% of sales. That sort of speaks to Slate's problem. It seems like folks would rather pay the extra money to not have to worry about range anxiety or charging up their cars as often.

Recent findings suggest that in reality, the EV3 isn't a direct competitor to the Slate, but Ford's yet-to-be-unveiled Fathom pickup is. It's expected to have a standard battery with around 250 miles of range and an optional battery with over 300 miles, Automotive News reports. Despite the fact it range-mogs the Slate, its starting price will come in at $29,945, including shipping, and it'll be an actual vehicle with the sort of modern luxuries and conveniences you'd expect in today's day and age.

According to recent reports, I'm not saying that the Slate is dead on arrival by any means, but I do think the Jeff Bezos-backed tech giant is really, really hoping that there are a lot of Quirked Up Individuals out there who will fall for the proletariat virtual signals of crank windows, no radio, a key you've got to insert and no screen while also paying a price that doesn't really connect with that reality. I'm not sure they're out there.
