#110909. New York Just Banned Subscriptions For Features Your Car Already Has

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (523 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

New York Just Banned Subscriptions For Features Your Car Already Has

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (523 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In-vehicle subscriptions are pretty universally maligned among car owners.
  • According to recent reports, the upcoming law, which takes effect on February 27, 2027, is part of a new section of the state's General Business Law, according to Spectrum News.
  • Hochul called the practice a "deceptive business model," according to CBS 6 Albany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In-vehicle subscriptions are pretty universally maligned among car owners. Most folks don't like the feeling of having to pay every month for features their cars were supposed to come with, and now New York State is doing something about it. Governor Kathy Hochul just signed a bill that bars automakers, dealers and their agents from selling subscriptions for features that are already installed.

According to recent reports, the upcoming law, which takes effect on February 27, 2027, is part of a new section of the state's General Business Law, according to Spectrum News. You can read the law for yourself here. It lays out fairly simple ground rules when it comes to subscriptions dealers or manufacturers can offer you: The feature must use hardware already in the car when it was bought or leased, and it must keep working without continual costs or support from the automaker or a third party. Those two things pretty much bring an end to crap like subscription-based heated seats and alike. It also is supposed to cover hands-off driving systems and enhanced navigation. Basically, once the hardware is physically in the car and the manufacturer isn't paying anything for you to use it, they can't then charge you. OEMs will also not be able to charge for software updates that fix safety defects.

Hochul called the practice a "deceptive business model," according to CBS 6 Albany. She also told automakers to keep their hands out of New Yorkers' wallets. It passed through the New York State Senate 57-3.

As with all good things, there are some exceptions. First of all, your lease or payment proposal doesn't count as a subscription, so don't even try it, slick.

The law also doesn't apply to navigation updates, infotainment features, satellite radio, in-vehicle WiFi, telematics, roadside assistance or "vehicle-connected services" that rely on cellular data or other networks, according to Motor1. It also exempts software-dependent driver assistance features, like Tesla's Full Self-Driving or GM's Super Cruise.

Recent findings suggest that I know what you're thinking. Didn't I just mention that hands-free driving systems are covered? Well, yes, but subscriptions tied to software and data are likely to survive, while hardware-only features are the real targets. Automakers will almost certainly make the argument that things like FSD and Super Cruise are "connected" or "software-dependent.".

One prime example of what this bill aims to get rid of is BMW keeping things like a 360-degree camera behind a paywall. That hardware is already built into the car, and, as we reported, it doesn't require a data connection to operate. It's the same thing with features like high-beam assist and remote start, so I imagine it'll be hard for BMW and other companies with similar schemes to argue that these are "connected." I mean, these are the same people who argue that buyers actually want subscriptions, which is certainly not true.

In any case, violators will face civil penalties of up to $250 per point-of-sale for each violation, though it's not clear exactly how that'll be counted. It's not clear if other states are going to follow suit, but here's hoping.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

In a recent development, artificial intelligence website builder 10Web Inc. is introducing a new feature that it claims can automatically turn content from Instagram, TikTok, Etsy, Google Business Profiles and more than 30 other sources into functioning websites and online stores.

Called Start from Anything, the feature targets small businesses that lack the time and expertise to build their own websites. Users can paste a link to an existing online presence or upload files, and 10Web’s AI extracts the information needed to construct a website.

The system can convert photos and videos into galleries and product pages, use captions to populate product descriptions, and turn service information into dedicated pages. Business hours, addresses and location information can automatically populate contact pages, while social media posts can become news items and promotional offers.

10Web stated its software also determines what functionality a website needs. Businesses offering services automatically receive booking capabilities, while those selling merchandise get online stores equipped to process orders and payments. Consumers can subsequently modify their websites by conversing with AI.

Recent findings suggest that “Nobody opens a bakery because they love choosing plugins,” Chief Executive Narek Torosyan said in a statement. “Every question we ask an owner about software is a question we failed to answer ourselves.”.

The service departs from the prompt-based approach that has dominated generative AI website development. Although prompts can create attractive websites, they require users to describe their businesses and often produce generic content that must subsequently be replaced or customized.

10Web’s approach is to reuse information businesses have already accumulated, such as photos, customer-facing descriptions, product catalogs and promotional materials.

The company remarked it tested the technology using publicly available content, converting a concept store‘s Instagram presence and a vintage retailer‘s TikTok account into online stores. It also generated websites from a vacation property‘s Google profile and a small business’s Facebook page.

The new capability builds on 10Web’s existing generative AI platform, which creates and manages websites using the open-source WordPress content management system.

In May 2025, the company introduced an application programming interface that allows developers and software providers to incorporate AI website generation into their applications. The platform uses specialized AI agents to handle different aspects of website development, including design, content creation and functionality.

10Web remarked the new feature includes hosting and is free to use for building and launching websites. The announcement did not specify charges for longer-term operation.

The firm said it serves tens of thousands of customers worldwide and attracts between 50,000 and 60,000 new signups monthly.

  • The Sienna's new hybrid powertrain has been totally recalibrated to operate the 2.5-liter four-cylinder at lower engine speeds when accelerating through the low and mid-range, and all Siennas now have a 1.15-kWh lithium-ion battery and a 166-horsepower electric motor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you're still hating on minivans in The Year Of Our Lord 2026, the joke is officially on you. Minivans are exceptionally versatile vehicles that are objectively the best option for most modern SUV buyers, but their lack of a perceived cool factor prevents many buyers from even considering them. We love minivans, and one of the most compelling minivans on the market today is the hybrid-only Toyota Sienna. It's getting even more compelling for 2027, since Toyota has bestowed it with some significant drivetrain improvements including the automaker's sixth-generation hybrid system that uses high efficiency electric motors, a retuned engine, and a more energy efficient lithium-ion battery.

According to recent reports, the 2027 Toyota Sienna isn't visibly distinguishable from the 2026 model since no changes were made to its exterior, but minivans have always been about what's beneath the skin, anyway. In addition to the new powertrain, all 2027 Siennas get the larger 12.3-inch infotainment screen and the larger 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster as standard, Toyota's latest suite of active-safety features, an integrated dash cam, a redesigned steering wheel and column, and new LED interior lights.

The Sienna's new hybrid powertrain has been totally recalibrated to operate the 2.5-liter four-cylinder at lower engine speeds when accelerating through the low and mid-range, and all Siennas now have a 1.15-kWh lithium-ion battery and a 166-horsepower electric motor. The powertrain produces a combined 251 horsepower, 6 more horses than last year, and Toyota reckons it's good for a 0.3-second quicker 0-to-60 sprint of 7.5 seconds in front-wheel-drive form. It can still be had with all-wheel drive, which adds a rear-mounted 54-hp electric motor, but its 0-to-60 time is actually a tenth slower than the front-drive model. Toyota now estimates both FWD and AWD Siennas will return 39 mpg in the city, 35 mpg on the highway, and 37 mpg combined, improvements of 3 mpg for FWD and 4 mpg for AWD.

Toyota notes the fresh steering system is more direct and has better on-center feel while reducing steering effort at low speeds for easier parking thanks to a new steering gear box, motor control unit, and torque sensor. The Sienna's brakes have also been reworked with a new electronic control system, offering improved feel and response with less body roll. The latest Toyota Safety Sense 4.0 suite of active safety features has upgraded sensors and hardware for improved obstacle detection capabilities, and in case that all fails, a built-in dash cam comes standard.

It has been revealed that other little changes include the cancellation of the Limited model, now leaving base LE, XLE, Woodland, XSE, and top Platinum trim levels. Toyota has not yet release pricing for the updated 2027 Sienna, but we expect its prices to increase slightly from their current starting point of $42,915.

Long Before The U.S. Air Force Existed, The Army Used Planes Made By The Wright Brothers

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The tactical advantage of holding the higher ground had been known for centuries, but aircraft opened up an entirely upcoming dimension.
  • Recent findings suggest that the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with how ubiquitous commercial air travel is today it's easy to overlook how astonishingly rapid early aircraft development was. There were only 24 years between the maiden flight of the Wright Flyer in 1903 and Charles Lindbergh made the first solo transatlantic flight in 1927. However, military thinkers were even quicker to realize the potential of powered flight on the battlefield. The U.S. Army purchased a Wright Military Flyer in 1909 for use as an observation aircraft. The first heavier-than-air military aircraft served as the spark that eventually led to creation of the U.S. Air Force, but it wasn't an unmitigated success.

The tactical advantage of holding the higher ground had been known for centuries, but aircraft opened up an entirely upcoming dimension. Initially, it was hot air balloons taking to the wild blue yonder. During the Civil War, the Union Army fielded a balloon corps to perform reconnaissance and scout Confederate Army positions. The corps wouldn't last long with then-General Ulysses S. Grant dissolving the unit in August 1863.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Army decided to revive this reconnaissance role when opening bidding for a two-seat observation aircraft in 1908. According to the U.S. Department of Defense, the Wright Military Flyer reached an altitude of 400 feet while averaging a speed of 42.5 miles per hour during its final ten-mile qualifying flight in July 1909. The service would purchase a single Wright Military Flyer for $30,000 next month. The sum would be $1.1 million today when adjusted for inflation.

The demonstration campaign that convinced the U.S. Army Signal Corps to open its checkbooks wasn't flawless. Orville Wright would bring a Wright Model A plane to Fort Myer near Arlington National Cemetery in 1908. The younger Wright brother flew dignitaries on brief flights around the Fort's drilling grounds in front of over 2,000 people.

The spectacle was going perfectly until First Lieutenant Thomas Selfridge climbed abroad as a passenger. He had been the first U.S. Army officer to fly a plane just months earlier. According to Air & Space Magazine, Model A suffered a propeller failure while flying at 40 mph at an altitude of at least 100 feet. The twin-propeller wood and canvas biplane tumbled out of control and plummeted to the ground. Wright was seriously injured, but the crash killed Selfridge.

In a recent development, in the crash's aftermath, a distraught Wright believed that he could've landed the plane safely if he had "a few feet more" of altitude. He returned to Fort Myer with an upgraded plane the next year and secured the sale to the Signal Corps. The Wright Military Flyer would never see combat, but it's easy to see how the early aircraft would've been vulnerable to machine gun fire from the ground with such a low maximum altitude. It wouldn't be the U.S. Army's last foray into experimental aircraft. The service would dabble in early drone warfare less than a decade later.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that let's ground your enthusiasm just a tad here.
  • To square up that giant publisher's musts, the vehicles are weighed on factors like how they perform on the site's road tests.
  • Consumer Reports also gives higher ratings for standard active safety tech.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that let's ground your enthusiasm just a tad here. Consumer Reports (CR) just came out with a list of a dozen 2026 models that right now offer steep Black Friday discounts. The organization is highlighting these deals because every whip on its list also received a strong overall score in Consumer Reports' testing. We have our own take on which vehicles we'd chase hardest, however, so we'll edit CR's edit.

To square up that giant publisher's musts, the vehicles are weighed on factors like how they perform on the site's road tests. And to earn a higher rating, cars that CR recommends need to have performed well in the owner surveys it conducts on hundreds of thousands of cars — the organization wants its readers to consider whether they'd buy the same car again if they had the chance. It also prefers vehicles that get better marks from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS).

Consumer Reports also gives higher ratings for standard active safety tech. This includes automatic emergency braking, blind-spot warning systems, and rear cross-traffic warning systems. And the publication gives props to vehicles that come with camera systems that monitor the driver for attentiveness. The outlet layers on extra credit if the IIHS states a car does well in its front crash protection tests for pedestrians. Consumer Reports' recommended rating also comes down to predicted reliability, again based on reader surveys.

Still, we've got our own take here, and we do a deeper dive on the discount fine print as well as sift their dozen choices down to an odd five cars — just because a car's cheaper doesn't mean you want it in the driveway for the next decade.

According to recent reports, the American-made Honda Ridgeline qualifies for some hefty incentives. Consumer Reports found discounts equaling up to $4,953. That's probably due to varied incentives offered by different dealers. For example, you can find $2,250 off via a national incentive directly from Honda, while Carsdirect demonstrates up to $2,750 off and 1.99% financing for 36 months. While a three-year loan means paying more per month than a longer term, 1.99% is far lower than the latest national average rate of 7.3% — meaning you'd be spending far less to pay off your Honda.

Sources indicate that poke around at area dealers, too. We found a deal offering at least $3,045 off of the Ridgeline, which actually exceeds the deal tallied by Consumer Reports, courtesy of Friendly Honda in Upcoming York's Hudson Valley. There's another way to save on the Ridgeline after you make the purchase. See, the truck is listed on Consumer Reports' top USA-made cars list, which could unlock some major loan deductions. The way that works is that if you purchase a qualifying American-made vehicle, the IRS gives you a tax credit of up to $10,000 on the interest paid on the loan for that new truck. On the Ridgeline, we arrived at a $5,633 in deductions.

Recent findings suggest that even without the tax credit, getting several thousand bucks off the Ridgeline makes it extra compelling. We praised its handling in our review of the off-road-focused Honda Ridgeline Trailsport, and we dig its ride quality. Ford's Maverick didn't make Consumer Reports' best cars made in America list, but this Honda wins for that, and we like it for out-towing the Ford, too.

Earlier this year, we put the Hyundai Elantra on our list of the cheapest new cars on the market for 2026. You, dear reader, also voted the Elantra onto your list of the best value cars, too. Consumer Reports found potential deals of up to $2,958 off the Elantra SEL's $23,950 MSRP before destination costs. Our own research demonstrates $2,000 back from Hyundai nationally, while some individual dealers such as Danbury Hyundai in Connecticut have an additional $500 available for recent college graduates and another $500 for first responders.

It has been revealed that as for why you like it — you actually prefer the Elantra Hybrid. The bummer there is that there's only a $500 discount off the $26,650 base price of that more fuel-efficient version of the Elantra. We get the thinking: We praised the Hybrid for being quieter and riding better than the non-hybrid, but don't forget that the base SE runs $24,120 with destination, before the $2,000 discount.

Recent findings suggest that previously, we praised the standard feature set, including an 8.0-inch touchscreen display, the fact that it gets standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and of course, Consumer Reports likes that it also comes baked with a blind-spot warning system, rear cross-traffic warning, and automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, as well as lane keeping. Oh, and if you're lanky, the Elantra easily fits taller drivers thanks to 40.6 inches of headroom and 42.3 inches of legroom.

Recent findings suggest that we don't know how Hyundai will price the next-generation Elantra – which feels too nice to be treated like an economy car. That may mean it won't be as affordable come this time next year, so you should probably buy one now, before prices climb.

Sources indicate that consumer Reports found savings of $4,852 off the 2026 Santa Fe. We found that Hyundai is offering a $3,000 national program plus 0% interest loans for up to 60 months, which is a very good way to save a lot of money on the carrying costs of a new car. Look around for other dealer incentives, too. We also found another $2,004 off offered by Ontario Hyundai in the Los Angeles area, knocking nearly $5,000 off the Santa Fe SEL's $40,075 sticker.

We dig the Santa Fe for lots of reasons. Back in 2024, we called it boxy and beautiful from every angle and praised Hyundai for moving from its frumpy curves to a more chiseled bod. Then there's the combination of utility — since it seats up to seven humans — and the fact that the interior is well designed and comfortable. We crowned it the crossover to end all crossovers, too, in part because we really love the dual-clutch transmission and the Santa Fe's superb ride.

If you're instead chasing fuel economy, Hyundai's $3,000 off the 2026 Santa Fe Hybrid is a better price cut than the carmaker's offering for the Elantra Hybrid. At $40,380, the 2026 Santa Fe Hybrid still pulls a significant premium over the non-hybrid, but you can qualify for the same 0% interest loan for 60 months.

In a recent development, audi's A3 and S3 are cars we can't help but drool over. That's partly because they're sports sedans, which is a dying breed. Audi is right now offering up to $3,500 off the sticker price of the A4 and $2,500 off the S3. That nudges the $41,495 A3's sticker (after destination) just beneath $40,000. However, the $53,395 S3 only gets a minor haircut.

Industry observers note that we noted back in 2025, when the Audi A3 and S3 underwent their most recent refresh, that that the cars are really petite — about three inches shorter than the Honda Civic. And yet we claimed that the Audi S3 is all the car you'll ever need. Our review of the S3 dovetails with why Consumer Reports likes the lower-tier A3, saying it outperforms peers like the BMW 2 Series Gran Coupe and Mercedes-Benz CLA. A base, 201-horsepower inline-four provides reasonable power in the A3, and while Consumer Reports doesn't love the car's dual-clutch transmission, we found this seven-speed gearbox delightful.

Note that this is a driver's car, first. We praised the driver's seat for its support, and so did Consumer Reports — but they handed a demerit to the squished nature of the rear perches. Did we mention it's smaller than a Honda Civic?

You can get up to $4,500 off the Rogue Platinum and $3,500 off lower-tier Rogues, but hunt a bit. We found $3,000 off a Rogue SV with a national incentive, plus another $950 from Poughkeepsie Nissan in New York. That knocked the total sticker down to $31,235. Then again, at a different dealer in Los Angeles, prices are sliding $3,000 across the table alongside $3,500 from Nissan, which drops the sticker of a Rogue SV from $32,500 down to $26,122. Even if you don't live in L.A., maybe it's worth flying out to buy that Nissan.

Sources indicate that as for the Rogue's attributes, they're good, if not revolutionary. The new-for-2027 Rogue Hybrid, however, is a total game-changer thanks to an entirely reinvented hybrid system, where we stated its silence speaks volumes, because it operates way more like a pure EV. That said, the 1.5-liter turbocharged inline-three beneath the hood of the 2026 Rogue is still plenty punchy, with 201 hp. Key to that sensation is low-end torque of 225 pound-feet hitting at 2,800 rpm and sticking around through 4,000 rpm.

Sources indicate that we noted that the Nissan's inline-3 delivers power more like what you'd expect from a larger V6, but the bonus is you're not pushing all those extra pistons. That means the FWD Rogue gets a combined 32 mpg while the AWD model gets 31 mpg. That's not the 38 mpg Nissan expects from its latest Rogue Hybrid, but if you can nab a 2026 Rogue for $26,000 versus the $37,065 tab on that latest-and-greatest Nissan, we're guessing you'll be just fine with that trade-off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rotterdam is expanding its methanol and ethanol business for industrial customers and ocean-going ships. Its inland freight fleet needs a different energy strategy. Confusing cargo, marine bunkering and propulsion would commit port authorities to parallel fuel networks when regular freight routes offer a stronger case for direct electrification.

Sources indicate that in May 2026, Tankmatch’s inland bunker vessel MTS Experience delivered certified biomethanol and second-generation ethanol to X-Press Feeders’ ocean-going Eco Levant. The fuels were transferred separately and blended aboard the receiving ship into 90% methanol and 10% ethanol. It was Rotterdam’s first ethanol bunkering of a seagoing vessel. The receiving ship burned the alcohol blend. The inland barge delivered it as cargo. Those are two different businesses.

It has been revealed that rotterdam had already confirmed an expansion of Evos’s Europoort terminal. Five storage tanks totaling 67,500 m³ are planned for methanol and ethanol, along with an inland-shipping berth scheduled for completion in early 2028. The berth includes shore power for vessels alongside. The project expands industrial storage, cargo transshipment and marine bunkering capacity. Developing an electric inland-freight corridor requires a separate charging and battery-service plan.

Low-carbon alcohols have a role in shipping services that still need liquid fuel. Aviation competes for oils and fats suitable for renewable diesel, leaving other sustainable feedstocks for marine alcohol fuels. I reassessed biomethanol’s role in the residual liquid-fuel market and examined alcohol-fuel generators as range extenders for hybrid ships. The investment test is lifecycle emissions, delivered fuel cost and demand from ships that need liquid energy.

The five planned tanks add 67,500 m³ of storage capacity across several markets. Rotterdam’s biomethanol bunkering grew from about 3,900 tons to almost 12,000 tons in 2025, according to the port authority. That is growth from a small base in the wider bunker market. Long-term investment still depends on recurring customers, contracted volumes and infrastructure utilization.

Ocean-going ships arrive with different engines, fuel contracts and routes. International ports will serve several bunker fuels for years. Los Angeles and Long Beach are approaching this market in stages, beginning with the fuels visiting vessels can buy and the commercial commitments needed for expansion. My assessment of those ports makes the same distinction between proving safe delivery and proving repeatable demand.

According to recent reports, inland shipping is a separate energy business. Many freight routes repeat between a limited number of ports and terminals. Charging equipment, onboard storage and battery exchange can follow sailing schedules, cargo cycles and terminal availability. A shared electrical network can serve dry cargo barges, chemical tankers and container vessels with different battery configurations and common interfaces.

My 98-page inland freight electrification report models five complete loaded-and-empty route cycles. A local port-canal shuttle requires 1.8 MWh, regional industrial service 4.3 MWh, irregular service 8.3 MWh, a major-port corridor 13.1 MWh and a long industrial corridor 36.8 MWh. These planning values precede vessel design margins. The twentyfold spread calls for different battery sizes, exchange frequencies and charging arrangements within a common electric propulsion system.

Some predictable services can charge fixed batteries during normal stops. Others benefit from exchangeable 20-foot battery containers, with smaller onboard batteries supplying hotel loads and resilience. Long corridors need reliable intermediate energy points. Hazardous-cargo tankers need cargo-pump integration, electrical segregation, fire protection and appropriate approvals. Those are problems of vessel design, safety approval and electrical infrastructure. Adding hydrogen, LNG and methanol supply chains adds costs of its own.

The Dutch Zero Emission Services model is already operating at modest scale. It lists five charging stations, two vessels in service and twelve conversion subsidies. Battery-container ownership and energy service can be separated from vessel ownership. Its shared interfaces demonstrate how multiple operators can purchase energy service from the same battery and charging network.

It has been revealed that the Central Commission for the Navigation of the Rhine records battery, hydrogen and LNG vessels, then argues that inland navigation has no universal propulsion solution. Its selected deployment database includes passenger vessels as well as freight. That inventory tells us which technologies have been tried. Comparing their economics and infrastructure costs is a separate task. Inland fleets can use varied hulls, battery sizes and charging arrangements while converging on electricity as the main propulsion energy carrier.

Port authorities need three distinct investment cases. Industrial alcohol storage needs chemical customers and cargo commitments. Marine bunkering needs ocean-going ship demand, fuel certification and contracts. Inland propulsion needs route-by-route electricity requirements, grid connections, terminal windows and a dependable energy service. Sharing port land and utilities can lower costs. Confusing the three markets can multiply them.

Sources indicate that rotterdam can expand methanol and ethanol handling while building a common electric backbone for inland freight. The barge carrying methanol does not need to burn it. Port investment should follow the service purchased by each customer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like missions and side quests, stealing cars has always been an integral part of the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise. For "GTA 6," not only have the developers leaned into advanced physics for more realistic car crashes, but car theft itself has evolved into multiple tiers.

While you can still do things the old-fashioned way, like pulling the driver out and taking control of the vehicle, or smashing a window, hotwiring the car, and driving away, those methods won't necessarily work on every car across the fictional state of Leonida. For example, keyless cars can't be hotwired. Even if someone left the doors of their expensive sports car open, you can't simply waltz in and drive away without a key cloner, which you'll only get access to later in the game. Standard and advanced vehicle trackers are also something to keep in mind. (Minor progression spoilers ahead.).

How can you tell if a car is keyless or has a tracker installed? Enter the WAiNK app. Your friend Cal installs it on your phone during a story mission in Chapter 1. The app lets you scan a car to see its make and model and whether it's locked, alarmed, keyless, or fitted with a tracker. Additionally, the app tells you the car's condition, how much it's worth, and what it costs to register should you wish to own it. Keep in mind that although registering stolen cars is how you take ownership of them in "GTA 6," that feature won't be unlocked until Chapter 2, when you meet Moses, who gifts you a slim jim.

It has been revealed that to steal cars without breaking the window or setting off the alarm, you'll need to use a slim jim. It works through a lock-picking minigame when you interact with a locked, unoccupied vehicle. While the method is unlikely to attract unwanted attention, it still won't let you start cars with keyless ignition. For that, you'll need to wait until you're about halfway through Chapter 3, at which point you'll get a key cloner. (It's a phone app you download during a story mission.).

The process itself is similar to using the slim jim, and once it's done, the door unlocks, and you drive away — no need to hotwire the car. As mentioned earlier, you can use the WAiNK app before you try to steal a car to see which sort of tracker it has, among other details. Standard trackers are not that big of a deal — the catch is that you can't take the car to a mod shop for any kind of modifications unless you've registered it as your own.

According to recent reports, cars with advanced trackers, on the other hand, alert the police and pinpoint your location — remember, "GTA 6" has flock-like cameras to track your movements. You'll have to drive really fast to stop the tracker from sending the location signal to the cops. If you slow down, the tracker starts beeping, and you only have a few seconds to speed up before it gives away your location. And, unlike in older "GTA" games, cars in "GTA 6" don't have infinite gas, so keep that in mind as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, coincidence is not causation, and yet the urge to ascribe causative power to random events is a typically human characteristic. Take the case of the man who snaps his fingers every five minutes. When a neighbor asks why, he replies, “To keep the elephants away.” “But there are no elephants anywhere around here,” the neighbor points out. “See?” the man states. “It’s working!”.

In a recent development, last week, people who rely on Microsoft Outlook to manage their lives suddenly found it was not working properly. The next day, the FAA issued a rare “ground stop” order because pieces of the digital system that air traffic controllers rely on failed.

Recent findings suggest that the following Monday, four of the country’s largest banks found their computer systems were malfunctioning, and United Airlines experienced a computer outage that exacerbated the travails of long suffering passengers still trying to recover from the “ground stop” fiasco. Then on Tuesday, the National Security Agency’s internal communications network went offline, and Apple web services were disrupted.

It has been revealed that according to the New York Times, Senator Josh Hawley, a Republican from Missouri, told reporters last week, “I think we ought to be briefed thoroughly on what is actually happening here. If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world.”.

It has been revealed that the president of the United States offered this reassuring statement: “It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and have all the money, things like this happen. It’s fine.”.

Not surprisingly, with all the talk about AI taking over the world and employees quitting their jobs to warn people of the danger, quite a few people are wondering if AI is responsible for all these digital disruptions.

In a recent development, for some Americans, the timing and scale of the outages made it hard to believe that sheer coincidence was the explanation. In a curious way, AI is involved, but not in the way you might think.

Sources indicate that ever since the digital revolution began more than 50 years ago, the computers we depend on have only been able to do what humans tell them to do. Those instructions are created by coders — people who use the programming language of the day that tell computers what to do and how to do it.

Industry observers note that it is well known in the trade that millions of lines of bad code exist. It is a phenomenon known as “garbage in, garbage out” or GIGO. Digital firms employ phalanxes of people to check the code their coders write, but it is a tedious process that often misses even glaring errors. Curiously, the most effective way to find bad code seems to be by using artificial intelligence, which can scan 10,000 times more lines of code in a given amount of time than a human can do.

According to recent reports, tech startup Calif remarked in a blog post this week that, using AI, it had found a critical flaw in Java4Shell, which leaves much of the internet exposed to cyber attacks if it is not corrected. Java is a popular programming language used by most Fortune 500 companies, according to Politico.

According to recent reports, “Banking, aviation, telecommunications, nearly every critical sector runs on Java, including national security systems,” Calif wrote. It calls Java “the beating heart of the modern economy.” Oracle, the developer of Java, released a patch for the vulnerability Tuesday. South Korea’s intelligence agency reportedly sent a separate security advisory earlier Tuesday to public institutions, warning them to fix the problem and prevent hackers from exploiting the Java flaw.

Industry observers note that the Java vulnerability comes weeks after a separate major vulnerability was discovered in another popular programming language, PHP, which powers up to 70 percent of the internet. At the time, governments worldwide advised organizations to take their sites offline to patch the vulnerability and prevent breaches.

According to recent reports, director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton mentioned on Fox News that ongoing efforts to patch the PHP vulnerability took an internal National Security Agency communications system offline Tuesday. He added that AI is making it easier to find such vulnerabilities, which can take years to fix without using the power of AI to find them.

Recent findings suggest that peter Avery is the chief information and security officer for Velocity Security, a cyber security firm in Michigan. He told the Fresh York Times he was skeptical that the events of last week were connected. “I like facts,” he remarked. “And until now, these are all separate problems.”.

Drawing patterns where they do not yet exist, he said, is human nature. It’s part of the need to make sense of things, he said, but can lead down a dark road. “When you start to live in that world where everyone’s a liar and no one is telling the truth, you are starting to live in fear.”.

According to recent reports, maybe snapping your fingers every five minutes is our best defense against cyber criminals stealing our data and crashing our online persona. That’s not a particularly comforting thought.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's little Tesla loves more than a dumb little party trick, and it often includes new gimmick functionality within major updates to its software. The recent release of V15, software for Tesla's latest in-car computers, adds another trick: A new camera angle that demonstrates the car from a third-person view, like in a video game. Tesla calls it Reality View, and out of everything a Tesla can do, it sure is one of the things.

Industry observers note that the Tesla faithful call the software revision V15, after the FSD version included, but the full package is known as Update 2026.38.6.11 — not exactly a name that rolls off the tongue. The update did include functional changes to FSD, mostly relating to the computer vision wall Tesla keeps beating its head against, but it seems the engineers had a thought while working on all those cameras: Why not use them to simulate a third-person view, like a video game?

FSD 15 can see chain link fence and power lines! 🤯🙌🏽 @Tesla @TeslaSI @elonmusk pic.twitter.com/m3fn7c4obA.

Initially, after looking at both Tesla's demo footage and footage from real owners, I figured the car was using SpaceXAI's models to generate a third-person view based on the input from the cameras — a method that would explain some of the odd glitches and scale issues present in some of the clips as AI hallucinations. According to Elon Musk's tweets, that's exactly what's going on — rather than an actual display of what the car's cameras and FSD software see, Tesla owners are now treated to an AI-generated picture of what's going on around them.

The ability to mesh multiple cameras into a single point of view like this is neat, and the underlying tech is impressive, though it's unclear how much compute is needed to generate these images, and what kind of load that puts on the car. What these images aren't, though, are replacements for the actual data visualization that FSD used to supply. Even Tesla owners are admitting confusion between objects the car does and doesn't see with the new display. Most Tesla party tricks are some ratio of neat to useless, but this one genuinely appears to make the user experience of FSD worse.

Breaking: Brava Security finds exposed log collectors could let attackers tamper with breach evidence

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A new report out today from security operations startup Brava Security Inc.
  • Dubbed “Ghost Feeds,” the research is said to show that attackers able to write into those collectors may be able to tamper with the evidence a security team uses to investigate a breach.
  • As part of the research, a decoy security information and event management system with no legitimate traffic was deployed on the public internet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Sources indicate that A new report out today from security operations startup Brava Security Inc. find that more than 2,300 exposed log collectors at nearly 1,200 organizations accepted fabricated security events without requiring credentials, raising questions about the reliability of the data that security teams depend on.

Dubbed “Ghost Feeds,” the research is said to show that attackers able to write into those collectors may be able to tamper with the evidence a security team uses to investigate a breach.

As part of the research, a decoy security information and event management system with no legitimate traffic was deployed on the public internet. Within about two hours, unknown parties had begun reading from the decoy. Attempts to inject fabricated events followed shortly after. The activity continued for at least two weeks.

Following on from the decoy, the researchers sent a single harmless, uniquely marked event to internet-exposed log collectors running any of seven logging products, including Elasticsearch, Splunk and Fluent Bit. More than 2,300 of those endpoints were found to accept the event with no authentication required. The number of organizations affected may be higher still, according to Brava, since its researchers were able to identify the owners of only about a third of the endpoints.

Recent findings suggest that results varied by platform, with about three-quarters of the exposed Elasticsearch clusters that responded accepting the test event. Nearly two-thirds of sampled TCP Syslog collectors also accepted it, as did 43% of identified Fluent Bit endpoints.

Splunk, the report notes, is a different story. Thanks to default authentication requirements, its HTTP Event Collector rejected 58% of test writes. The catch is that the primary forwarding port on a standard Splunk installation was shown in laboratory testing to accept unauthenticated events in plain text. More than 100,000 internet hosts listen on that port number, with 42% of a sample accepting the unauthenticated events.

According to the researchers, the damage from forged telemetry can go well beyond false alerts. In one lab test, 13 cents’ worth of bandwidth generated enough data to exceed a Splunk daily license allowance by 2.39 times in 141 seconds. Should that happen repeatedly, search can be disabled while logs continue to come in, potentially leaving a security team unable to investigate.

“Security teams cannot afford to assume that everything appearing in their SIEM is trustworthy,” stated Idan Basre, Brava’s co-founder and chief executive, who led product management for Microsoft Defender before starting the company. An attacker able to influence that evidence, he warned, could potentially “change the outcome of an investigation before anyone realizes the underlying data has been compromised.”.

According to recent reports, brava’s researchers also wanted to know what manipulated logs would do to AI-powered security operations. To find out, three popular open-source AI security operations center tools were given the same suspicious login scenario.

All three initially identified the activity correctly. Once the researchers had injected 10 fabricated Windows events into the logs, the same suspicious login went unnoticed by all three.

Since AI investigators are “only as reliable as the evidence they analyze,” according to Brava co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Itay Gabbay, attackers able to write into the systems supplying that evidence may be able to influence what security teams and their AI agents end up dismissing.

Sources indicate that to help organizations check their own exposure, Brava is releasing ghost-telemetry-check, a free, open-source tool designed to test whether a logging pipeline will accept unauthenticated events. Detection rules for Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel and other platforms are also included in the release.

Brava formally rolled out earlier this month with $15 million in seed funding led by F2 Venture Capital and Pitango Venture Capital. Its platform is remarked to use multi-agent AI to generate the telemetry an attack would produce without carrying out the attack, showing companies which threats their existing defenses would miss.

At $7,999, Is This 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia A Beautiful Bargain?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 1970s band Nazareth warned us that Love Hurts.
  • Legend has it that, though the execs at Land Rover tasked company stylist David Bache with designing the bodywork of the in-development Range Rover, they were so taken with the styling of the engineering mules that, with minor tweaks, that became the truck's first and final design.
  • In a recent development, the 1987 Range Rover Classic we looked at on Tuesday differed from that original design with a modified grille and, more importantly, four doors, as the earlier two-door model was never offered for sale in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 1970s band Nazareth warned us that Love Hurts. Today's Nice Price or No Dice Alfa Romeo has looks that could make you fall in love, but also a brand reputation for tempestuousness that might cause pain — financial and otherwise. Let's find out if this one is priced to make that pain hurt so good.

Legend has it that, though the execs at Land Rover tasked company stylist David Bache with designing the bodywork of the in-development Range Rover, they were so taken with the styling of the engineering mules that, with minor tweaks, that became the truck's first and final design.

In a recent development, the 1987 Range Rover Classic we looked at on Tuesday differed from that original design with a modified grille and, more importantly, four doors, as the earlier two-door model was never offered for sale in the U.S. Our Range Rover was claimed to have been restored, and while there remained some boogers under its desk, it did look to be in serviceable overall shape. That wasn't enough to get the vast majority of you on board with the idea of spending the $28,850 the seller asked for its sale. Ultimately, that price fell in a 93% 'No Dice' loss.

In a recent development, I'd like to get one thing out of the way up front: I find today's 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia incredibly good-looking, with no bad angles from which to view it. I mention that because my prose describing the car might be a bit biased by the siren's song of the car's Helen-of-Troy-build-a-big-horse-beat-up-the-Trojans level of good looks.

Of course, like Helen's legendary beauty and the battles fought by suitors for the opportunity to awkwardly sit at her knee and stare stupidly into her limpid pool eyes, owning an Alfa Romeo of any ilk could lead to devastation.

Industry observers note that alfa had to get the Giulia's looks just right, a necessity that went so far as to delay the car's launch. Fiat boss Sergio Marchionne kept rejecting designs Alfa's internal Centro Stile Alfa Romeo designers offered during the car's development, claiming they weren't good-looking enough. Why Alfa didn't go the route of having a design house like Pininfarina pen the car is a mystery, although traditionally Alfa handled saloon styling in-house while farming out coupes to such esteemed external designers, so there's that.

Regardless, Alfa got the Giulia's looks right, and didn't screw up the car's underpinnings either. Rolling on a then-upcoming RWD platform developed with oversight by Ferrari engineer Philippe Krief, the Giulia has the goods to compete with the likes of BMW's 3 Series and Audi A4 when the roads get bendy. It's a testament to how good the basic chassis is that it can perform competently with this base four-cylinder model and, with notable tweaks, also with the monster 500-horsepower V6 Quadrifoglio.

Our car has the 1,995cc DOHC MultiAir four under the hood. With variable valve timing and an intercooled turbocharger, that makes an astounding 280 hp and 306 pound-feet of torque. Matched to that engine is a ZF 8HP50 8-speed automatic transmission that powers the rear wheels. While AWD was offered on this model, this car's RWD layout is simpler to maintain and lighter, offering better performance and fuel economy.

According to the ad, this Giulia has 75,000 miles on the clock and, remarkable for any Alfa, especially a first-year model that may still be suffering teething pains, it is claimed to suffer no problems whatsoever. Did I mention it's also really good-looking?

Industry observers note that having established that this is a very attractive car, it's also in very good shape. The pictures in the ad support the seller's claim that it's "well kept," as the Silverstone Gray Metallic paint appears to have no dents, and the darker gray factory alloys show no evidence of curb rash.

This being an entry-level model and with the ad's limited description, the seating surfaces are likely vinyl rather than leather. Some wood on the console warms up the space in an otherwise Germanic, all-black (even the Alfa badge) interior.

In a recent development, that's not to say that the car is parsimoniously equipped, as it has all the basic comfort and convenience features one might expect on a reasonably modern car. Those include power windows, locks, seats and mirrors, dual-zone climate control with eyeball vents for the back seats, and a center stack screen for infotainment and the backup camera display. There's also cruise control, auto headlamps... You name it, it's likely got it.

It has been revealed that per the seller, the car presents in excellent condition, has a clean title, and drives perfectly. What more could one want?

In a recent development, well, I'm sure one thing we could all ask for is a car that's free and can navigate to a leprechaun's pot of gold when asked. There are certain things we can't have, no matter how much we want them.

This car isn't free, but its $7,999 asking price is a recent reduction from $8,500, and it makes one wonder: just how scared are people about buying a decade-old, out-of-warranty Alfa that even that slightly higher price seemingly couldn't get a nibble?

Naturally, you'll suss it out in the comments and, ultimately, judge it in the vote. With that in mind, what's your take on this base-but-far-from-basic Giulia and that new, lower $7,999 asking price? Is that a handsome deal on this beauty of a car? Or, even at that modest amount, could buying this Alfa get ugly real fast?

San Diego, California, Craigslist, or go here if the ad disappears.

What Car Are You Glad Is Dead?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that from an objective standpoint, cars are difficult things to justify.
  • Sources indicate that you've likely said the same thing to yourself, which brings me to today's question: I want to know which car you're glad is dead.
  • Sources indicate that I'm taking the most obvious route here and saying that I'm glad the Tesla Cybertruck is dead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that from an objective standpoint, cars are difficult things to justify. They are prohibitively expensive to buy, fuel, insure, maintain, and repair. They pollute, they kill pedestrians (and people in other cars), and they are a categorically flawed form of mass transportation. They are also really interesting, exciting, fun, private, and convenient, and in many parts of the real world, they're often a necessary component of daily life. It can feel like a complex duality to hold the love of cars in tandem with an understanding of their downsides, but doing so has made me appreciate every car on the road. Having said that, every now and then I'll see a car on the road and think, "thank goodness that's not being made anymore.".

Sources indicate that you've likely said the same thing to yourself, which brings me to today's question: I want to know which car you're glad is dead. Whether it's a personal vendetta against a certain model that ran over your RC car as a kid, or a model that drained your wallet and tested your patience when you owned it, share your answer in the comments section below.

Sources indicate that I'm taking the most obvious route here and saying that I'm glad the Tesla Cybertruck is dead. Though it's technically not slated to end production until next year, I'm counting it because it is such a hateful vehicle, it deserves the accolade. Sometimes I wonder if the Cybertruck would've been received as cool in an alternate reality where Tesla's CEO isn't a cringey spoiled megalomaniac loser, but I guess the world will never know.

In the context of our present reality, everything about the Cybertruck came off as a tarnished middle finger to the idea of sensibility, rationality, and logic, as well as a middle finger to every other road user, thanks to the sharp edges of its stainless steel body panels. If you think I'm being dramatic, know that its edges are so sharp, in fact, that the United Kingdom refused to issue the Cybertruck a certificate of conformity to the UK's vehicle safety standards. UK police publicly seized a Cybertruck that someone was illegally using on British roads, saying, "whilst this may seem trivial to some, legitimate concerns exist around the safety of other road users or pedestrians if they were involved in a collision with a Cybertruck.".

Recent findings suggest that I feel like the world will be a better place once the Cybertruck is out of production, so I'm glad it's dead. What car are you glad is dead?

Tech Report: Autos Are Still The Sticking Point In The U.S.-Canada Trade War

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that good morning!
  • and Canada are still at odds on auto tariffs as the trade war continues, an ex-Volkswagen engineer pleads guilty to inside trading over the company's deal with Rivian, Stellantis is suing the Unifor union for alleged "obstruction" of environmental work at Brampton plant and Amazon Autos is heading to the UK.
  • With everything else going on in the world at the moment, you'd be forgiven for forgetting that there's an entire trade war happening between the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that good morning! It's Wednesday, November 25, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most vital stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.

In this morning's edition, the U.S. and Canada are still at odds on auto tariffs as the trade war continues, an ex-Volkswagen engineer pleads guilty to inside trading over the company's deal with Rivian, Stellantis is suing the Unifor union for alleged "obstruction" of environmental work at Brampton plant and Amazon Autos is heading to the UK.

With everything else going on in the world at the moment, you'd be forgiven for forgetting that there's an entire trade war happening between the U.S. and Canada right now, but I'm here to remind you that bad boy is still raging. Much of that is thanks to auto tariffs — one of the major sticking points dividing the two North American countries as negotiations heat back up following a last-minute collapse this summer.

Recent findings suggest that automotive and other key industrial sectors, like steel, are holding up a deal that could end the two-year trade war. President Trump enacted a 25% tariff on auto imports in April of 2025, and Canada came right back with its own in-kind duties soon after. It's a real mess, and it's driving up costs for everyone. Obviously, this didn't need to happen. Trump didn't need to do this, but here we are. From Automotive News:.

Industry observers note that both sets of tariffs include exemptions for locally made parts, which lowers the effective tariff rate on Canadian vehicles exported to the United States to about 12.5 per cent and U.S. exports to Canada to about 21.25 per cent — though the exact rate varies by plant and model.

In a recent development, trump has repeatedly claimed the United States does not need Canadian-made cars and pressed automakers to shift production south of the border. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has maintained that any agreement with the United States must leave Canada with a viable auto sector.

Ottawa has been pushing for a deal that will put the effective tariff rate for Canadian vehicle exports to the United States on an even keel with those built south of the border but has been hard-pressed to get there, [Automotive Parts Manufacturers' Association president, Flavio] Volpe remarked.

As negotiators closed in on a deal this summer by pitching a broader parts exemption, the U.S. offer would have left Canadian autos facing up an effective tariff of up to 7.5 per cent tariffs, he said. While an improvement over the roughly 12.5 per cent rate automakers face today, it is still higher than the industry's profit margin, making it too high for Ottawa to accept, Volpe added.

Canadian negotiators are "not religious" about what mechanism is used to bring the effective tariff rate down, Volpe said, but want to put plants on both sides of the border back on an even playing field.

Counterintuitively, U.S. assembly plants are not immune to tariffs.

It has been revealed that parts compliant with the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement reach U.S. assembly lines tariff-free, but American-made vehicles compliant with the trade deal can include 25 per cent parts content from overseas. That content faces up to 25-per-cent tariffs, translating into a tariff rate on U.S.-made vehicles of as much as 6.5 per cent.

It has been revealed that A 3.75-per-cent MSRP credit for American-made vehicles offered by the U.S. Department of Commerce — effective through 2030 — offsets part of these added costs.

Sources indicate that but even automakers building USMCA-compliant vehicles in the United States can face an effective tariff rate of 2.75 per cent. The tally can be more or less, depending on where companies source their parts.

The five automakers that right now produce vehicles in Canada — the Major Three, Honda and Toyota — are pushing hard for an interim deal that would close or eliminate the tariff gap between Canadian and U.S. plants, even if it's a short-term solution.

Recent findings suggest that right now, there's no real timetable for when a deal could be reached, though Canadian pundits are actually aware that Trump has threatened to hike tariffs to 50% at the start of 2027. While they don't think it'll happen, with Trump, it can never be truly ruled out.

Recent findings suggest that A former Volkswagen engineer pleaded guilty to insider trading based on secret information he possessed about the automaker's planned $5 billion joint venture with electric vehicle maker Rivian. Michael Stamp pleaded guilty to securities fraud in a Manhattan federal court as part of a deal with prosecutors, confessing that he used his brokerage accounts to buy Rivian shares and options while in possession of confidential information about the merger that he had learned from another employee.

As we previously reported, the 31-year-old and another former VW engineer, Marcus Plank, were charged in July with making a combined $300,000 trading before the Rivian deal was unveiled publicly. Prosecutors said Stamp made a cool quarter million, and Plank made $50,000 while also passing information to a family member who made $12,000. From Bloomberg:.

"I knew that what I was doing was wrong and a breach of my duty to my employer," Stamp remarked at a hearing before a federal judge.

Volkswagen and Rivian declared the deal on June 26, 2024, giving Rivian a financial lifeline as manufacturers large and small began to rethink strategies in a slowing market for electric vehicles.

It has been revealed that stamp and Plank, who were both living in San Jose, California, while on assignment from Germany, were initially charged with conspiracy and securities fraud and faced as much as 25 years in prison if convicted of the most serious counts at trial. Plank has pleaded not guilty and is free on a $500,000 bond.

In a recent development, prosecutors remarked internet searches made around the time of the crimes revealed that the two men knew what they were doing was illegal. Just eight days before the announcement, Stamp — that goofus — searched for "statute of limitations insider trading," according to the government. Soon after, Plank's aforementioned family member searched in German "how is insider trading prosecuted?".

Well, massive dog, this is how it's prosecuted — unless you're very rich or in Congress.

In a recent development, there's another fun chapter in the war over Stellantis' Brampton Assembly plant in Ontario, Canada. Now, it's spilled over into court as the automaker has filed a lawsuit against the Unifor workers' union, alleging it is impeding an environmental assessment necessary for the sale to defense contractor Roshel to go through.

Recent findings suggest that in documents filed in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, Stellantis mentioned it is seeking an injunction that would require the union, its national president Lana Payne and Unifor Local 1285 plant chairperson Ardis Snow to stop blocking the Brampton plant and preventing work at the site. The manufacturer wants the court to declare that the union has trespassed at the facility and "obstructed the lawful entrance to and exit from the premises." From Automotive News:.

A statement of claim remarked union officials are "physically preventing, impeding, and restricting Stellantis' ability to provide access to the premises" to environmental consulting firm Pinchin Ltd.

Sources indicate that pinchin was retained by Roshel — the armoured vehicle manufacturer that agreed to buy the idled Brampton plant from Stellantis for an undisclosed amount earlier this month — to carry out environmental work starting Nov. 9, according to the documents.

However, Stellantis said that morning, union representatives blockaded entrances to the plant with trucks, pylons and individuals carrying Unifor flags and that Unifor told the automaker it wouldn't let Pinchin personnel or equipment through.

"To date, Unifor has continued to obstruct access by persons associated with the environmental work, and Pinchin has not been permitted to perform the environmental work," the statement of claim mentioned.

"Despite Stellantis' reasonable efforts to obtain police assistance, those efforts have not brought the obstruction of or interference with lawful access to the premises under an acceptable degree of control, nor has Pinchin been permitted to access the premises.".

The allegations have not been tested in court.

The statement of claim said Stellantis "is suffering and will continue to suffer irreparable harm and other losses," although the extent of those losses "are extremely difficult, if not impossible, to quantify in monetary terms.".

It added that "continued obstruction" of the environmental assessment "threatens to delay or prevent completion of a material diligence step, interfere with the timetable for the proposed transaction, and affect the responsibilities of Stellantis and Roshel following closing of the proposed transaction.".

Stellantis' deal with Roshel is expected to close in mid-December, subject to certain conditions, according to the documents.

In response, Unifor remarked it has been "demonstrating in support of Canadian jobs at the Brampton plant throughout the past year." Payne said that the sale of the plant to Roshel is "unacceptable" to the union, and it will continue to work with all parties to get a different outcome.

Sources indicate that amazon Autos isn't satisfied with taking on just the U.S. automotive industry, so it has turned its attention to the United Kingdom. Early next year, customers in the UK will be able to buy a new car right on Amazon.com. It'll be the first time the U.S.-based e-commerce giant expands its auto services to an overseas market. As it was in the U.S., the first brand to team up with Amazon Autos in this endeavor is Hyundai. From The Wall Street Journal:.

With the Amazon Autos platform, customers will be able to browse real-time dealer inventory, see upfront pricing, get an instant trade-in valuation, connect with a local dealer, as well as reserve a car, the statement said.

Hyundai's IONIQ series as well as its i20 and KONA models will be available on the platform. More brands and dealer partners will be declared before its launch.

According to recent reports, around $1.3 trillion of cars were sold by dealerships in the U.S. last year, according to the National Automobile Dealers Association.

Amazon Autos was first launched in December of 2024, and the program has expanded to over 150 cities in that time, and it now sells vehicles from 35 brands. I'd expect a similar sort of expansion in the U.S. in due time.

The neat trick with Amazon Autos is that you can sort of use it how you want to. Some customers use the platform from start to finish, visiting the dealership just to pick up the vehicle. However, some start the process on Amazon and then visit the dealership to apply for financing or finish the process. Amazon may be, uh, bad, but I do appreciate that sort of choice and flexibility.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s been the expectation for months, since SpaceX’s IPO at least, that Tesla and SpaceX will merge.
  • Well, far beyond suspicions, reporting implies that this is really going to happen, and may even be on the verge of happening.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Musk mentioned on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call last month ​that a merger unifying his AI, robotics, EV and aerospace ambitions ​under a single corporate roof would be ‘a good idea,'” Reuters also noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s been the expectation for months, since SpaceX’s IPO at least, that Tesla and SpaceX will merge. The suspicions haven’t been built on a lot of evidence, more so just the sense that this is what Elon Musk would like to do — including because it would give him basically unchecked control of the combined company (more so than he already has).

Well, far beyond suspicions, reporting implies that this is really going to happen, and may even be on the verge of happening. The Financial Times reports that Tesla and SpaceX have appointed a total of five directors from their boards to explore the possibility — three directors from Tesla’s board and two from SpaceX’s board. In fact, we even know the people who have been appointed — Robyn Denholm (Tesla), Kathleen Wilson-Thompson (Tesla), Jack Hartung (Tesla), Roelof Botha (SpaceX), and Randy Glein (SpaceX).

Recent findings suggest that “Musk mentioned on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call last month ​that a merger unifying his AI, robotics, EV and aerospace ambitions ​under a single corporate roof would be ‘a good idea,'” Reuters also noted. “He confirmed that the companies had formed special committees of independent directors to discuss ​a union.”.

In a recent development, when this idea first came up, the significant issue that was raised is that Tesla is heavily dependent on China — for both sales and production — and SpaceX is a key military supplier. China could, therefore, put strong pressure on the firm to make it do what China wants. SpaceX would, in essence, be compromised. Whether or not there’s a way around that or it matters in this era of Trump’s massive corruption, I don’t know. Just look at what has happened and is happening with NVIDIA — the CEO (Jensen Huang) was having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, NVIDIA then went ahead and did what China wanted it to do (with the support of President Trump, whom NVIDIA’s CEO heavily supported), Huang was forced out of NVIDIA after it was revealed he had been having an affair with this spy (as well as other people, including employees), and now he’s been welcomed back to NVIDIA after Trump said a few things and the board had a long, heart-to-heart talk with Huang. With that story in mind, not to mention the insane levels of corruption Trump and his family have been engaging in, is the Trump administration going to have any issue with the national security concerns that would be raised from Tesla and SpaceX merging?

We’ll see what happens, but at the moment, it sure looks like a merger is on the horizon.

#110876. Tesla Is Not The Only Automaker To Join The Space Race

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1123 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla Is Not The Only Automaker To Join The Space Race

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1123 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Intertubes are practically bursting at the seam with news of another step towards the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, both of which are helmed by on-again, off-again Trump supporter Elon Musk.
  • Before you get too excited, Ford is not exactly taking over the space business, nor is it necessarily competing against SpaceX.
  • Alongside its newly minted minority ownership status, the automaker will apply its manufacturing experience to help kickstart Revolution’s spacecraft platform into volume production.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Intertubes are practically bursting at the seam with news of another step towards the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, both of which are helmed by on-again, off-again Trump supporter Elon Musk. Buried beneath the avalanche of press is another automotive-aerospace mashup, that being Ford Motor Firm’s newly confirmed investment in the US startup Revolution Space. Evidently the iconic automaker is particularly interested in Revolution’s “unique in-space propulsion technologies.” Hmmm…interesting!

Before you get too excited, Ford is not exactly taking over the space business, nor is it necessarily competing against SpaceX. Revolution specializes in spacecraft, not rocket introduces. In addition, Ford is not merging itself with Revolution. On November 23, Ford confirmed that it is taking up a minority stake in the startup for a yet-to-be-disclosed sum, through its Industrial Platform LLC subsidiary.

Alongside its newly minted minority ownership status, the automaker will apply its manufacturing experience to help kickstart Revolution’s spacecraft platform into volume production.

So, what does Ford have that Revolution wants? Apparently, lots. “With Ford’s manufacturing capabilities, the companies are partnering to industrialize Revolution Space’s next-generation spacecraft at scale, unlocking new dynamic missions and proliferated constellations,” Ford explained in a press statement.

Ford’s Chief Strategy Officer, Marin Gjaja, also chipped in his two cents, emphasizing that “Ford’s strength is building complex products in large volumes, something today’s growing satellite market requires.”.

Industry observers note that gjaja also underscored Ford’s immediate interest in the matter, which is to diversify and harden itself against the shifting winds of the global auto market — presumably including the abrupt shift in federal energy policy here in the US, too. As cited by Ford, the “space economy” presently registers about $600 billion globally, which is peanuts compared to the $1.8 trillion anticipated by 2035.

“Increasingly scaled satellite manufacturing is one of the drivers of that growth,” Ford further explains, noting that the firm Future Market Insights estimates the global satellite manufacturing market in the range of $87–$114 billion by 2035, heads and shoulders above the current estimate of $22–$26 billion.

Industry observers note that if all goes according to initiative, Revolution Space will give the automaker a hand in government and commercial satellite applications. Ford lists communications, Earth observation, navigation, space domain awareness, satellite servicing, and scientific and deep-space missions among the areas of interest. One can  safely assume that military applications are in there somewhere, too.

It has been revealed that as for what Ford may expect in return in terms of technology transfer, that remains to be seen. Ford notes that its experience in the aerospace field includes building communications and weather satellites for NASA and the military here in the US, as well as NATO.

However, that work goes back 50-60 years ago. The satellites of today are a different creature. “Revolution Space delivers and operates advanced space systems with superior performance and propulsion technologies designed to achieve the precision control and sustained maneuverability to enhance existing and create new, high-value, dynamic missions,” Ford notes.

In the November 24 announcement, Ford also notes that it has deployed its manufacturing experience to pivot into fresh fields as called for, citing the bombers it built during World War II and, more recently, the ventilators and protective equipment it supplied during the outset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Drones could be next on the menu. Coincidentally or not, on November 24, the Wall Street Journal reported that Ford is in the running to help supply drones to the Department of Defense, alongside General Motors among other stakeholders. If realized, the program would call for supplying actuators, engines, sensors, lidar and other elements to drone manufacturers.

“Defense Department leaders have spent months enlisting automakers and their well-established supply chains to help scale up production of everything from missiles to tactical trucks. Now, they want those companies to help ease shortages of unmanned systems, including surveillance and strike drones, that have become crucial in global conflicts,” WSJ elaborated.

In a recent development, good luck with that. Don’t expect anything of consequence to materialize until Defense Secretary Pete Hesgeth leaves office, either voluntarily or by virtue of impeachment over the hash he has made of the Defense Department, including its equipment as well as its personnel.

Still, the WSJ report did yield an interesting nugget about Ford’s minority stake in Revolution Space. For those without a subscription, the Detroit Free Press kindly offers a summary citing Ford spokesperson David Tovar, who said that Ford has “had discussions with the Pentagon” focusing on its recent investment in Revolution Space, as well as the manufacture of vehicles for the military.

That’s a good question. The Revolution website is rather thin on the technology itself, though it does note that the board is chaired by former NASA administrator Daniel Goldin, with former NASA astronaut Paul W. Richards serving as Chief Engineer and Chief Strategy Officer.

Revolution does drop a few hints about its expectations for the manufacturing hookup with Ford. The company notes that in 2025 it was selected for the DARPA “LASSO” program, with DARPA being short for the Defense Advanced Research Agency.

DARPA describes LASSO as a program aimed at “significantly increasing the United States’ ability to conduct operations in support of space situational awareness by developing both autonomous satellite navigation in stressing orbital conditions and increasing satellite maneuverability through continuous dynamic repositioning based on changing conditions, with the added benefit of creating a proven reserve model for resources relevant to ISRU on Earth’s Moon,” with ISRU being short for in-situ resource utilization.

In a recent development, if you guessed water on the moon is the aim, run right out and buy yourself a cigar. “The program seeks performers to design, test, build, and deliver a spacecraft capable of determining all areas on the Moon that contain greater than 5% water concentration,” DARPA explains.

The LASSO selection comes on the heels of a flurry of activity in 2024, when Revolution reported that it was awarded a slot in the “Advanced Capabilities & Demonstration Missions” program of the Defense Innovation Unit. DIU also deployed its fast-track authority under the “Other Transactions” program to tap Revolution for an award in support of the company’s responsive modular electrospray thrust technology.

In 2024 Revolution Space also reported that it earned an award from the Defense Department’s “Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies” program, and it nailed down an agreement with NASA to collaborate on space technology.

As for the Tesla-SpaceX merger, if you have any thoughts about that drop a note in the comment thread.
